text: More about active play with pawns
zh: 进一步谈兵的积极行动

text: The pawn wedge and the reaction to it. The pawn nail. The phalanx of e- and f-pawns. Pawn storm.
zh: 兵楔及其应对。钉子兵。e兵与f兵组成的兵阵。兵风暴。

text: And so we have convinced ourselves that the role of the pawn in no way amounts to positional pressure, the control of squares of a certain colour, securing a handy base for piece forces; the pawns are also a powerful 1 means of attack. Without active pawn support, a piece attack often turns out to be doomed to failure, running up against a defensive bristle of enemy pawns. Consequently, one of the main attacking tasks of pawns is the removal of the opponent's defensive pawn line in the sector serving as an object of a planned attack. If, however, such a pawn attack is launched against castling, then it often leads to the creation of direct mating threats to the exposed king.
zh: 前文已经说明，兵的作用不仅在于施加局面压力、控制某种颜色的格，或为子力提供便利的据点；兵本身也是强大的进攻力量。缺少兵的积极支援，子力的进攻往往会受阻于对方的兵屏障，最终失败。因此，兵在进攻中的主要任务之一，就是清除预定攻击区域中的防御兵线。若兵的攻击指向对方易位后的阵地，还常能暴露敌王，制造直接的将杀威胁。

text: In practice, with active pawn operations, well known is the formation in the centre bearing the graphic name pawn wedge. The scheme of "driving" such a wedge appears in the following form.
zh: 在兵的积极行动中，有一种常见的中心兵形，形象地称为“兵楔”。下图展示了这种兵楔楔入对方阵地的形态。

text: (see diagram next column)
zh: （见下一图。）

text: It should be noted that the formation e4-d5-c4 (for Black e5d4-c5) is called a wedge in the case when one of the opponent's pawns, adjacent to the wedging pawns, is still on its original square c7 or e7 (c2 or e2). Such a wedge is more dynamic (prospects of advancing c4-c5 or e4-e5 for White, correspondingly ... c5-c4 or ... e5e4 for Black), but in return less stable in view of the possibility of undermining it by the moves ...
zh: 应当指出，e4-d5-c4（黑方为e5-d4-c5）兵形称为兵楔时，楔入兵两侧相邻的对方兵，至少有一个仍留在原始格c7或e7（相应为c2或e2）。这种兵楔具有更强的动态潜力：白方可以冲起c5或e5，黑方则可冲起c4或e4。但它也较不稳固，因为对方可以用以下冲兵加以冲击：

text: c7-c6 or ... e7-e6 (c2-c3 or e2-e3).
zh: ...c7-c6或...e7-e6（白方相应为c2-c3或e2-e3）。

text: The undermining advance of the f-pawn serves as the basic method of struggle against the wedge. A careful assessment of the position will determine whether the construction of the wedge is favourable or unfavourable. The wedge, of course, allows the gain of space and cramps the opponent, but at the same time limits the dynamic resources and, uo the contrary, increases them for the enemy due to clear prospects of a lively pawn action on the king's flank. It is hardly worthwhile constructing a wedge just to somewhat cramp the opponent. The construction of a wedge is justified only in that case when it is possible to count on retaining the initiative or at least where there is the possibility of preventing the advance of the enemy f-pawn.
zh: 冲起f兵打击兵楔的根基，是对抗兵楔的主要方法。建立兵楔是否有利，必须仔细判断具体局面。兵楔固然能争取空间、压缩对手的活动，却也会减少己方的动态选择；对手反而有了在王翼积极运用兵的明确方向。仅仅为了稍微压缩对手，通常不值得建立兵楔。只有能够保持主动权，或至少有办法阻止对方冲起f兵时，这种兵形才有充分依据。

text: White more often has recourse to a pawn wedge than Black. In several ideological variations of the King's Indian Defence or Spanish Game, it is a logical link in the plan of play.
zh: 白方采用兵楔比黑方更常见。在古印度防御和西班牙开局的若干典型变化中，建立兵楔是整体计划中合乎逻辑的一环。

text: The author of one interesting plan, entailing the construction of a wedge, in the King's Indian Defence, was Nimzovich. In his game with Tartakover (Carlsbad 1929) after
zh: 尼姆佐维奇曾在古印度防御中构思过一个以兵楔为基础的有趣计划。在1929年卡尔斯巴德的尼姆佐维奇对塔塔科维尔一局中，以下走法之后形成了下图局面：

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. f3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nc3 O-O 6. Be3 Nbd7 7. Nh3
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. f3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nc3 O-O 6. Be3 Nbd7 7. Nh3

text: e5 the following position was reached.
zh: e5

text: Here, Nimzovich played 8. d5, on which followed 8... a5.
zh:
尼姆佐维奇走了：

**8. d5 a5**

text: Black's plan consists of placing his knight on c5, for which its position is secured against the raid b4, and then transferring the other knight to h5, d7 or e8 and beginning conventional play on the basis of the undermining move ... f5. Such a plan has led to success time and again.
zh: 黑方准备把马调到c5，先阻止白方以b4驱逐它；然后将另一马调往h5、d7或e8，再以...f5冲击兵楔，展开通常的反击。这一计划曾多次取得成功。

text: White pins the knight down to f6 and, in that period while Black will be trying to free himself from the pin, he intends to launch an energetic pawn offensive on the king's flank. This outlines Nimzovich's plan.
zh: 白方牵制f6马，准备趁黑方设法摆脱牵制时，在王翼发动有力的兵的攻击。这就是尼姆佐维奇计划的要点。

text: As indicated by Nimzovich himself, Black, on the 10th move, should have continued 10... Nh5
zh: 尼姆佐维奇本人指出，黑方第10步应走10... Nh5，

text: and, if 11. g4, then 11... Nf4! 12. Bxf4 exf4 13. Qxf4 f5 14. gxf5 gxf5
zh: 若11. g4，则11... Nf4! 12. Bxf4 exf4 13. Qxf4 f5 14. gxf5 gxf5；

text: and 15. exf5 is bad in view of 15...
zh: 15. exf5不好，因为15...

text: Black has not succeeded in playing ... f5, while on the king's flank it is White who is attacking. In these circumstances, the construction of the wedge is more than justified.
zh: 黑方未能走成...f5，反而是白方在王翼发动进攻。在这种情况下，建立兵楔显然很有道理。

text: 14. h5 gxh5 15. Bxf6 Bxf6 16
zh: 14. h5 gxh5 15. Bxf6 Bxf6 16.

text: Rxh5
zh: Rxh5

text: From now on the h5 and f5
zh: 从此，h5和f5

text: squares prove to be excellent bases for White's pieces, and on this foundation he gains victory.
zh: 两格成为白方子力的优良据点，白方以此为基础赢得胜利。

text: After this game, the idea of the wedge, with the future attack of the h and g-pawns, found widespread application in chess practice.
zh: 此局之后，先建立兵楔，再以h兵和g兵发起进攻的构想，在实战中得到广泛应用。

text: Makogonov-Smyslov, Sverdlovsk 1943, saw a similar plan:
zh: 1943年在斯维尔德洛夫斯克的马卡戈诺夫对斯梅斯洛夫一局，也采用了类似计划：

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. e4 e5 5. d5
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 d6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. e4 e5 5. d5

text: And so, without hesitation, White goes for the wedge. Many would prefer here to fight to maintain the tension in the centre by continuing 5. Nf3. Likewise, a good plan of development was 5. g3, followed by Nge2 and Bg2, trying to retain the d5 square as a point for a possible piece invasion.
zh: 白方毫不犹豫地建立兵楔。许多棋手在这里会选择5. Nf3，保持中心的紧张状态。5. g3后Nge2、Bg2也是良好的出子方案，保留d5作为子力可能进驻的据点。

text: Nc56. f3a57Be3 Be7 The development of the bishop to g7 makes no sense in the light of White's plan. The latter's arrangement of pieces is virtually the same as Nimzovich's in the previous game.
zh:
**5... Nc5 6. f3 a5 7. Be3 Be7**

针对白方的计划，把象出到g7没有意义。白方的子力配置，与上一例尼姆佐维奇的布局几乎相同。

text: Black must do something about the wedge which is hampering him. True, for the present there is nothing threatening the Black king since its pawn cover is still in its original position, but there is a way for White to further develop his initiative, for example the man0euvre Ng1-e2-g3-f5. Risky is
zh: 黑方必须设法应对这个限制己方活动的兵楔。眼下黑王尚无危险，因为掩护它的兵仍在原始位置；但白方可以用Ng1-e2-g3-f5等运马方案扩大主动权。以下走法有风险：

text: 13. Bf2, and White, winning back the pawn, maintains active chances on the open h-file.
zh: 13. Bf2，白方吃回一兵，并在开放的h线上保持积极机会。

text: 11. O-O-O cxd5
zh: 11. O-O-O cxd5

zh: 最好立即走11... a4，随后...Qa5，继续向d5施压。

text: 12. Nxd5 Be6 13. Ne2 Bxd5 14. exd5 a4
zh: 12. Nxd5 Be6 13. Ne2 Bxd5 14. exd5 a4

text: Clearing the centre (14... e4 15
zh: 打开中心对白方有利。例如14... e4 15.

zh: fxe4 Nxe4 16. Qc2 Nc5 17. g5 f6 18.

zh: Kb1，白方占优。

zh: 15. Nc3 Qa5

zh: 此时15... Bxh4仍有危险，因为16. g5 Bg3 17. Ne2。

text: The d5 pawn remains standing and severely cramps Black.
zh: d5兵仍牢牢站住，严重限制黑方的活动。

text: Black has a weak pawn configuration on the queen's flank and this prompts him to avoid exchanges. In fact, after 16. Qxd2+ 17. Rxd2 b6 18. Bd3 White has a powerful position and the a4 pawn is doomed.
zh: 黑方后翼兵形薄弱，因此力避兑换。若16... Qxd2+ 17. Rxd2 b6 18. Bd3，白方局面强大，a4兵难逃被吃的命运。

text: 17. Qf2 Rd8 18. a3 Nc7 19. Bxc5
zh: 17. Qf2 Rd8 18. a3 Nc7 19. Bxc5

text: Leading to a forced win of the a4 pawn.
zh: 强制赢得a4兵。

text: 19... dxc5 20. Nc3 Qa5 21. Bd3 b5 22. Qc2 bxc4 23. Bxc4
zh: 19... dxc5 20. Nc3 Qa5 21. Bd3 b5 22. Qc2 bxc4 23. Bxc4

text: Also good enough is 23. Bxh7+
zh: 23. Bxh7+ Kh8 24. Qf5 Ne8 25. Ne4也足够了。

Rdg1

zh: 28. Bd3 g6 29. Rdg1后冲起h5更有力。

text: Preparing 31. Bd3, which at once would be repulsed by the reply 30... f5.
zh: 准备31. Bd3。若立即走Bd3，黑方则可用30... f5化解。

text: The only defence against Bd3, but now White without difficulty wins the endgame in which he has, in addition to an extra pawn, also a positional superiority due to the excellent piece base on e4 and the passed pawn on d5, which is the consequence of the opening construction of the wedge. The remaining part of the game is of no interest for our theme; Black resigned on the 54th move.
zh: 这是应对Bd3的唯一办法，但白方现在可以轻松赢下残局。他不仅多一兵，还拥有e4据点和d5通路兵带来的局面优势，而后者正是开局建立兵楔的成果。余下过程与本章主题无关；黑方在第54步认输。

text: In the following game White went in for the wedge, ignoring the conventional reaction ... f5. It was not long before the latter began to tell.
zh: 下一局中，白方建立兵楔时忽略了常见的...f5反击，很快便尝到了后果。

text: Bogolyubov-Indian Defence
zh: 波戈印度防御

text: White: V.Alatortsev
zh: 白方：V.阿拉托尔采夫

text: Black: G.Levenfish
zh: 黑方：G.列文菲什

text: (10th USSR Championship 1937)
zh: （1937年第10届苏联锦标赛）

text: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 Bxd2+ 5. Nxd2
zh: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 Bxd2+ 5. Nxd2

text: The black-squared bishops have been exchanged. This circumstance must have a certain bearing on the opponent's plans.
zh: 双方黑格象已兑掉，制定计划时必须考虑这一点。

text: 5... Nc6 6. Ngf3 d6
zh: 5... Nc6 6. Ngf3 d6

text: Black prepares ... e5, which fully conforms to the exchange of bishops: it is precisely the black squares in the centre which the pawn takes under control. The other plan with n ... d5 was less logical and made it difficult for Black to develop his queen's flank.
zh: 黑方准备...e5，这完全符合兑象后的局面要求：这个兵所控制的正是中心黑格。另一项以...d5为核心的计划不够合乎逻辑，而且会妨碍黑方完成后翼出子。

text: Here this wedge form of invasion has little foundation. It might have some justification if White were to succeed later in beginning a headlong advance in the centre by playing e4 and f4. The wedge ought to cramp Black, but here the basic motive of the cramping restriction of the activity of the king's bishop - is absent. Moreover, with the move d5 White actually limits the sphere of action of the king's bishop, only not the enemy's but his own. He should continue 8. e3 exd4 9. Nxd4 Nxd4
zh: 这里建立兵楔缺乏依据。除非白方接着能走e4、f4，在中心迅速发起冲击，否则很难证明其合理性。兵楔本应限制黑方，但最重要的一项作用——限制对方黑格象——在这里并不存在。白方冲起d5，反倒限制了自己白格象的活动。他应走8. e3 exd4 9. Nxd4 Nxd4，

text: 10. exd4 Qe7+ 11. Qe2 or 8. Nb3
zh: 10. exd4 Qe7+ 11. Qe2 或 8. Nb3

text: Qe7 9. e3, maintaining relative equilibrium.
zh: Qe7 9. e3，保持大致均势。

text: Even now, 10. e3 was better, so as, for example, on 10... c6 to play 11. dxc6 bxc6 12. Qc2 followed
zh: 即使此时，10. e3仍更好。例如10... c6 11. dxc6 bxc6 12. Qc2，随后

text: by Rad1 or 11... Nxc6 12. Qe2 d5 13. cxd5 Nxd5 14. Rfd1. 10... Nd7

Black obviously intends to carry out ... f5. White also should construct his plan, bearing in mind this possibility; after ... f5 he can take the pawn and, exploiting the e4 square as a piece base, strive for play on the queen's flank with the move c5.
zh: 黑方显然准备...f5，白方制定计划时也应据此安排：待...f5后吃兵，以e4为子力据点，再用c5在后翼寻求反击。

text: He does not have a moment to lose, since after Nd3 White threatens counterplay by f4.
zh: 黑方不能再耽搁，因为白方准备Nd3后以f4反击。

text: Again played without regard for the opponent's plan. It was necessary either to take the pawn on f5, followed by Ne4, or even decide on f4. After 12... exf4 13. gxf4
zh: 白方再次忽略对手的计划。此时必须在f5吃兵后走Ne4，或干脆决定冲起f4。12... exf4 13. gxf4之后，

text: fxe4 14. Nxe4 Nf515 Nc2,
zh: fxe4 14. Nxe4 Nf5 15. Nc2，

text: weaknesses appear for White, but they can be defended.
zh: 白方虽有弱点，却仍能防守。

text: In this way Black develops an initiative and at the same time prevents White's prepared f4.
zh: 黑方借此夺取主动权，同时阻止白方准备好的f4。

text: 13. gxf4
zh: 13. gxf4

text: This exchange is by no means forced. True, if White does not take this pawn, then after ... Ng6 it threatens to turn into a pawn "wedge", driven into the opponent's position. However, after 13. f3 h5 or the comparatively better
zh: 这次兑换并非被迫。白方若不吃这个兵，黑方接着...Ng6，确实有把它变成深入白方阵地的“兵楔”的可能。不过，13. f3 h5，或相对更好的以下变化之后：

text: Kg7 16. Nf3 h6 17. Bf5 Qe8, despite having the worse position he retains possibilities of defence. But now Black obtains a firm piece base in the very centre of the board - the e5 square, on the basis of which he eventually achieves victory. In this light, the opening construction of the wedge looks especially doubtful for White.
zh: Kg7 16. Nf3 h6 17. Bf5 Qe8，白方虽然略差，仍有防守余地。实战中，黑方却在棋盘正中心获得了稳固的e5据点，并以此为基础赢棋。由此反观白方开局建立兵楔的决定，就更加可疑了。

text: 13... exf4 14. Nf3 Ng6 15. Rc1 Qe7 16. Re1 Nde5 17. Nfxe5 Nxe5 18. f3 b6 19. Nxe5 Qxe5
zh: 13... exf4 14. Nf3 Ng6 15. Rc1 Qe7 16. Re1 Nde5 17. Nfxe5 Nxe5 18. f3 b6 19. Nxe5 Qxe5

text: After ... Bd7, Black threatens to begin a decisive pawn offensive on the king's flank with the moves ... g5 and ... h5. White hastens to force the exchange of queens, but this also does not help much.
zh: 黑方准备...Bd7后，以...g5和...h5发动决定性的兵的攻击。白方急于强制兑后，但这也无济于事。

text: 20. Qd2 Bd7 21. Qc3 Rfe8 22. Qxe5 Rxe5 23. a3 a5 24. b3 Kf7 25. Kf2 Kf6 26. Ke2 Rh5 27. Rh1
zh: 20. Qd2 Bd7 21. Qc3 Rfe8 22. Qxe5 Rxe5 23. a3 a5 24. b3 Kf7 25. Kf2 Kf6 26. Ke2 Rh5 27. Rh1

text: Ke5 and White lost after Black had carried out the advance ... g5-g4, since even at the moment of surrender the notorious c4-d5-e4 wedge was still standing intact in all its splendour. In conclusion we look at a few games where the question of the wedge is elucidated in the light of a single planned process.
zh:
**Ke5**

黑方完成...g5-g4后，白方输掉了对局。讽刺的是，直到认输时，c4-d5-e4兵楔依然原封不动地留在中心。

下面再看几盘对局，从完整计划的执行过程考察兵楔的作用。

text: Reti Opening
zh: 列蒂开局

text: White: J.R.Capablanca
zh: 白方：J.R.卡帕布兰卡

text: Black: F.Marshall
zh: 黑方：F.马歇尔

text: (Moscow 1925)
1. Nf3 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5 4. b3 c5 5. Bg2 Nc6 6. O-O Be7
zh: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5 4. b3 c5 5. Bg2 Nc6 6. O-O Be7

text: Both now and in the future, White not only is not afraid of the construction of Black's wedge, but even provokes it on ... d4. There are, however, chessplayers who do not like to contend with the triangle of pawns in the centre and prefer 7. cxd5 Nxd5 (if 7... exd5, then 8. d4 with play on the isolated d5 pawn) 8. Bb2; after 8... Bf6 the activity of both the White bishops is appreciably limited.
zh: 白方现在以及此后都不怕黑方建立兵楔，甚至有意诱使对方走...d4。不过，有些棋手不愿面对这样的中心兵三角，更喜欢7. cxd5 Nxd5（若7... exd5，则8. d4，针对d5孤兵展开行动）8. Bb2；但8... Bf6后，白方双象的活动会受到明显限制。

text: 7. d3 O-O 8. Bb2 d4
zh: 7. d3 O-O 8. Bb2 d4

text: One can judge the extent of the difference of opinion, held even by leading chess authorities, about the role of the wedge, by the fact that one of the commentators of the present game,F Bogolyubov, placed exclamation mark an against this move, adding "it is clear that White's ( opening has been strategically refuted'. Capablanca obviously held another point of view.
zh: 即使顶尖棋手，对兵楔作用的看法也可能大相径庭。评注本局的波戈留波夫就给这步加了感叹号，并写道：“显然，白方的开局已在战略上遭到反驳。”卡帕布兰卡显然另有看法。

text: A problem move! White wants to provoke the reply y ... e5 and then begin to prepare the break f4, which serves as a reliable means of contending with the wedge. This, of course, does not mean that he will without fail gain the advantage if he fulfils such a plan. When White plays f4, Black must be ready to reply to it ... exf4, and, after gxf4, f5. The further course of events might turn out something like this: 9... e5 10. a3
zh: 这步向黑方提出了一个问题：白方想诱使黑方走...e5，再准备f4冲兵突破，这是对抗兵楔的可靠办法。当然，执行这一计划并不保证白方必然占优。白方走f4时，黑方应准备...exf4，待gxf4后再...f5。可能的后续进程如下：9... e5 10. a3，

text: a5 11. Nbd2 Bd7 12. Qc2 Ne8 13. Rae1 Qc7 14. Kh1 Nd6 15. Ng1 Nd8 16. Ne2 Ne6 17. f4 exf4 18. gxf4 f5 19. e5 Nf7 20. Ng3 Nh6
zh: a5 11. Nbd2 Bd7 12. Qc2 Ne8 13. Rae1 Qc7 14. Kh1 Nd6 15. Ng1 Nd8 16. Ne2 Ne6 17. f4 exf4 18. gxf4 f5 19. e5 Nf7 20. Ng3 Nh6

text: followed by ... Bc6, and Black has a right to cherish hopes of success in the struggle for the initiative.
zh: 随后...Bc6，黑方有理由期待在主动权的争夺中取得成功。

text: Alas, Marshall chooses another way, which radically contradicts the opening g idea of the wedge construction.

text: On the board are opposite coloured bishops. In the endgame this often serves to guarantee a draw even when t the opponent has a considerable e material advantage. On the other hand, in the middlegame the presence of opposite coloured bishops quite often makes it easier for the attacking side to achieve victory. Meanwhile, he has a black-squared bishop which comes up against a barrier everywhere, in the shape of its own pawns. Another matter is the opponent's bishop, centering fire on the white squares which are the most important main lines on the board. If we add to this the fact that Black has a weak pawn on f6, his king is insecurely placed, its last cover - the h7 point - exposed to attack, and the enemy rooks dominate the weak white squares in the region of the king's flank, then it becomes clear that White has achieved a decisive advantage.

text: King's Indian Defence

text: White: L.Polugayevsky

text: Black: A.Suetin

text: (25th USSR Championship 1958)

text: This is a long-standing way of playing against the King's Indian Defence for White, and has recently become more and more frequently met in practice. It is wellknown that in his return match with Smyslov, Botvinnik likewise stuck to this treatment of the opening. The apparently very modest move of the f-pawn has great planning significance. It extends far beyond the limits of a simple striving to reinforce one of the main links of the pawn centre - the e4 pawn. White's plan consists of the construction of a wedge with a subsequent meeting of the counterattack ... f5 with g4. If Black refrains from ... f5, then he will not only turn out to be severely cramped by the wedge, but White will also have the possibility of developing a dangerous pawn attack on the king's flank by h4-h5. All these ""trumps" are exploited by White in the present game.
zh: 这是白方对付古印度防御的一种古老方案，在本书写作时期又越来越常见。鲍特维尼克对斯梅斯洛夫的世界冠军回敬赛中，也采用了这一思路。看似温和的f兵一步，具有深远的计划意义，远不只是巩固中心支柱e4兵。白方准备建立兵楔，再以g4应对...f5反击。若黑方不走...f5，不仅会被兵楔严重压缩，还可能遭到h4-h5发动的危险的兵的攻击。本局白方充分利用了这些有利条件。

text: If Black does not take measures to determine the position in the centre, then, after Qd2 and O-O-O, White without difficulty develops a threatening attack on the king's flank (g4, h4-h5, Bh6) under the cover of the pawn centre. With this it becomes clear that Black submits to the construction of the opponent's wedge, intending, even after g4, to sharpen the game with the advance e ... f5.
zh: 黑方若不尽快明确中心局面，白方Qd2、长易位后，就能在中心兵群的掩护下，以g4、h4-h5和Bh6轻松组织危险的王翼进攻。因此黑方接受白方建立兵楔，准备即使白方走了g4，也仍用...f5把局面引向尖锐的斗争。

text: In his last match with Botvinnik, Smyslov tried to counter White's plan with energetic pawn play on the queen's flank (... a6, ...c6, and ... b5). This counterattacking idea has still not received sufficient practical trials; in any event it did not justify itself in the match.
zh: 在当时最近一次与鲍特维尼克的对抗赛中，斯梅斯洛夫曾试图以...a6、...c6和...b5在后翼积极冲兵，反击白方的计划。这一构想尚缺少充分的实战检验，至少在那次对抗赛中没有奏效。

text: Such a blockade of the c4 pawn is usually linked to an attack on the pawn wedge from the side of the queen's flank. Black strives in the future for ... a6 and ... b5. In the present game it does not come to this and the move ... c5 loses its clearness of purpose.
zh: 用兵封锁c4，通常是为从后翼攻击兵楔作准备：黑方接着争取...a6和...b5。但本局并未实现这一计划，因此...c5显得目的不明。

text: This position eloquently bears witness to how contemporary notions have changed concerning the opening struggle. According to classical principles, the principal opening task has still not been accomplished: the pieces are virtually undeveloped, it is mainly the pawns which have advanced (White's will make 7 moves out of the first 10!). And yet, despite the opinion of some opening theoreticians, the opening stage can be considered over. The plans of the opponents, particularly White, are determined, but the struggle of the plans - is already a process of the middlegame.
zh: 这个局面鲜明地说明，开局观念已经发生变化。按经典原则，开局的主要任务尚未完成：棋子几乎都没有出动，主要走的是兵，白方前十步中竟有七步走兵！不过，尽管有些开局理论家不同意，我们仍可认为开局已经结束：双方，尤其是白方的计划已经明确，而计划之间的交锋，已是中局的内容。

text: The diagrammed position was reached in two more encounters in the same tournament, i.e.: Tal- Boleslavsky (played earlier than the present game) and Kotov- Spassky (played later). The first ended in a victory for Black, the second - for White; admittedly these results could only be attributed to a small extent to the opening.

text: The threatening destructive force contained in pawn attacks can show itself not only in groups of pawns but also in a single pawn, particularly when we have the business of the so-called pawnnail. With this we have in mind a pawn which breaks through to the
zh: 兵的攻击所蕴含的破坏力，不仅能通过兵群，也能通过单个兵表现出来，尤其是所谓“钉子兵”。它指的是一个冲到

text: 6th (for Black - the 3rd) rank and establishes itself on it. It can indeed be compared to a nail, hammered deeply into the position of the enemy forces.
zh: 第六横线（黑方则是第三横线）并牢牢站住的兵，犹如一枚钉子，深深钉入对方阵地。

text: If the wedge, that is a pawn consolidated on the 5th rank, cramps the opponent, then the nail on the 6th rank pins down his forces and serves as a support for the most dangerous attacking pieces.
zh: 第五横线上的兵楔能够压缩对手的活动，而第六横线上的钉子兵则能束缚对方子力，为最具威胁的进攻棋子提供支撑。

text: We illustrate this statement with some examples.
zh: 我们用一些例子来说明这一说法。

text: White's plan is determined. Under the cover of the pawn-nail, pinning down the opponent, he intends to come down upon the Black king's position with his superior forces. With his last move, White eliminates one of the Black knights covering the castled position. Black is not in a position to repulse this onslaught. The reserves on the queen's flank, held back by the pawn-nail, do not succeed in getting across to help.
zh: 白方的计划已经明确：利用钉子兵束缚对手，以优势兵力进攻黑王。这步消灭了一匹保护黑王的马，黑方已无力抵挡。后翼子力被钉子兵挡住，也来不及赶来援救。

text: 9. h3 followed by d4 is met more frequently in contemporary practice. The modest (in appearance!) move chosen by White in the present game does not mean giving up the advance of the pawn to d4; it only postpones this advance to a later time, with the intention of preparing it more thoroughly. However, such a slow tactic also opens up t the possibility for Black of a harmonious mobilisation of forces and therefore it is no surprise that the present variation is met comparatively rarely.
zh: 在本书写作时期，9. h3后d4更常见。白方实战这步只是表面温和，并未放弃冲起d4，而是推迟行动，先作更充分的准备。不过，这样缓慢的下法也让黑方有时间协调出子，因此这个变化较少出现，并不奇怪。

text: The development of the queen's bishop on the long diagonal in this variation is not very well grounded. The activity of the bishop is very limited due to the d3 and e4 pawns; however the main defect of this idea consists of the dangerous weakening of the f5 square, precisely towards which the knight heads along the routemarch Nf1-g3-f5.
zh: 在这个变化中，把白格象出到长斜线上缺乏依据。d3兵和e4兵会严重限制它的活动；更主要的问题是危险地削弱了f5，白马正可以沿Nf1-g3-f5的路线进驻。

text: Black had several comfortable continuations, out of which 12... Be6 deserved the most consideration.
zh: 黑方有几种稳妥的后续手段，其中12... Be6最值得考虑。

zh: 13. Nf1 Qc7 14. Ng3 g6

zh: 黑方不能允许白马进驻f5，只得在王翼留下一个令人不安的弱点。

zh: 15. Bg5 Rad8 16. axb5 axb5 17. Qc1 Rfe8 18. h3

text: The beginning of a great plan of attack, at the basis of which lies the advance of the f-pawn.
zh: 一个庞大的进攻计划由此开始，其核心是冲起f兵。

text: If we recall Black's 15th move then this could be regarded as a very clear loss of tempo. In fact this is not so. White has opened the a-file e and this radically changed the situation, so Rubinstein thought, rather to his advantage in so far as White's intended activity on the king's flank can be countered by play on the a-file by
zh: 联系黑方第15步来看，这步似乎明显浪费了先手，其实并非如此。白方打开a线后，局势发生了根本变化。鲁宾斯坦认为这对自己有利：他可以沿a线反击白方的王翼行动，例如...

text: Rxa1 followed by ... Ra8. 19
zh: Rxa1，随后...Ra8。19.

text: Qd2 Ra5 and ... Rea8 does not
zh: Qd2 Ra5再...Rea8，

text: change matters.
zh: 也不会改变局势。

text: And yet this consideration is not well founded. White's plan consists of a transfer of the knight to g4, where it will attack the weakened f6 and h6 squares, but mainly of the advance of the f-pawn.
zh: 不过，这一判断缺乏依据。白方准备把马调到g4，攻击f6和h6弱格，而计划的核心仍是冲起f兵。

text: A careful look at variations connected with the execution of this plan shows that his threats are created quite quickly. Therefore White voluntarily y concedes the a-file, concentrating all his efforts on an attack of the castled position.
zh: 具体分析表明，白方能够迅速制造威胁。因此，他主动让出a线，把全部力量集中到对黑王易位阵地的进攻上。

text: With this exchange, White retains his queen in the centre, from where it would have been diverted in the event of Rxa1, and at the same time diverts one of Black's pieces, the bishop or rook, from defence of the king's flank.
zh: 这次兑换使白后留在中心；若让黑方先...Rxa1，白后便要被牵离中心去吃回。同时，黑方必须把象或车中的一枚调离王翼防守。

text: What can Black do against this dangerous offensive? Apart from the reply 21... Ne8, chosen by Rubinstein and proving to be insufficient for defence of the weaknesses in the castled position, Black has available two plans of defence.
zh: 黑方如何应对这一危险攻势？鲁宾斯坦实战选择21... Ne8，却不足以保护易位阵地中的弱点。除此以外，黑方还有两种防守计划。

text: The first is based on the move 21... exf4, which on the face of it is bad since Black himself opens an artery of attack on the f7 point and helps the enemy queen to get on to this artery. Another plan consists of maintaining the pawn tension "f4-e5" and leaving White to decide whether to eliminate this tension by the exchange fxe5 or to further advance the f-pawn to f5.
zh: 第一种是21... exf4。表面看这步不好，因为黑方主动打开了通向f7的进攻线路，还帮助白后进入这条线。另一种是维持f4与e5之间的兵的对峙，让白方决定是fxe5解除紧张，还是继续冲起f5。

text: With the second plan, the most purposeful move seems 21... Bd7 in order to include the rook in the defence of the king's flank. However, careful analysis shows that after 21. Rf1 with the threat fxe5 the future struggle must turn out unfavourably for Black. On 22... Qd8, which incidentally once again cuts off the rook from the king's flank, possible is 23. f5 Kg7 24. Ng4, and it is difficult to defend the f6 point. However, the continuation 23... h5 (instead of 23... Kg7) with the aim of preventing the knight from going to g4, is unsatisfactory in view of 24. fxg6
zh: 后一计划中，21... Bd7最有针对性，可以让车参加王翼防守。但仔细分析表明，白方Rf1并威胁fxe5后，黑方仍将陷入不利。若22... Qd8，又把车与王翼隔开，则23. f5 Kg7 24. Ng4，f6很难守住。若以23... h5代替23... Kg7阻止Ng4，也不行，因为24. fxg6，

text: fxg6 25. Bxf6 Bxf6 26. Qh6!
zh: fxg6 25. Bxf6 Bxf6 26. Qh6!。

text: Both these variations and the actual course of the game convince one that it is dangerous for Black to allow the advance f5. There remains to look concretely at the consequences of the "bad" reply 21. exf4. Further events would probably have developed like this:
zh: 这些变化以及实战进程都说明，允许白方冲起f5十分危险。因此，还应具体考察那步看似不好的21... exf4。可能的变化如下：

text: 21... exf4 22. Qxf4 Qd8 23. Rf1
zh: 21... exf4 22. Qxf4 Qd8 23. Rf1

text: Kg7; then Black could reinforce the f7 point by the move ... Ra7; if 24. Ne2, preparing d4, then possible is 24... Bd7 25. d4 exd4 26. cxd4 Be8 with new defensive resources, since the knight f6 is freed from defence of the f7 point. Of course, White gets an initiative but he does not obtain that forcing attack which he obtains in connection with f5.
zh: Kg7，黑方随后可用...Ra7保护f7。若24. Ne2准备d4，则24... Bd7 25. d4 cxd4 26. cxd4 Be8，黑方又有新的防守资源，f6马也不再需要保护f7。白方固然掌握主动，却无法像冲起f5后那样发动强制性的进攻。〔校勘注：原书25... exd4应为25... cxd4；黑方e兵已在21... exf4时离开e线。〕

text: On the basis of Rubinstein's plan of defence, the following ideas come out of his actions: the exchangeC of the black-squared bishops (clearing the atmosphere), the concentration of three defenders on the f6 point - the king, the knight, the queen - against three possible White blows: the queen and rook on the f-file and the knight from the g4 square. And yet with this he does not take into account the weakness of the h6 square, which likewise serves as an object of White's attack. However, allowing the pawn nail on the f-file, which in the end will be hammered in on the f6 square, proves to be a decisive help to this attack.
zh: 从鲁宾斯坦的行动可以看出，他准备先兑掉黑格象，缓解压力，再把王、马、后三枚子力集中保护f6，以应对白方可能投入的三枚攻击子力：f线上的后、车，以及g4马。但他忽略了h6也是白方的攻击目标。更严重的是，他允许白方在f6钉下一兵，而这将对进攻起决定性作用。

text: Now White e threatens to increase the pressure by Rf1 followed by Ng4-h6+.
zh: 白方准备Rf1，随后Ng4-h6+，进一步加强压力。

text: 22... Bxg5 23. Qxg5 Qe7 24. Qh6 Qf8 25. Qc1 Qg7 26. Rf1 g5
zh: 22... Bxg5 23. Qxg5 Qe7 24. Qh6 Qf8 25. Qc1 Qg7 26. Rf1 g5

text: This move, which furthermore gives White the h5 point (and you see that this is an approach to the critical f6 square), makes it easier for his opponent to carry out the attack. The stubborn most defence, preventing the hostile knight rampaging on the weak squares of the king's flank, was 26... h5, but also in this case White has a very strong initiative. Possible is 27. fxg6 fxg6 28. Nf3, invading on g5, or 27. Qd1 with the threat 28. fxg6 fxg6 29. Bb3+.
zh: 这步又让出h5——白马通向关键格f6的跳板——使白方更容易展开进攻。最顽强的防守是26... h5，阻止白马利用王翼弱格。不过，白方仍有很强的主动权，可以27. fxg6 fxg6 28. Nf3，准备侵入g5；也可以27. Qd1，威胁28. fxg6 fxg6 29. Bb3+。

zh: 钉子兵终于钉进阵地。黑方现在可以认输了：黑王完全孤立，已没有子力能够赶来救援。

zh: 讨论兵风暴之前，先看看e兵、f兵并列组成的兵阵，以及围绕它展开的整体行动计划；这里e兵所在的线上没有对方兵。

text: Here we have a position from Rubinstein-Marshall, Lodz 1908. White's phalanx is ready for a decisive break e6 or f6. Events developed like this:
zh: 图中是1908年在罗兹的鲁宾斯坦对马歇尔一局。白方兵阵已准备好以e6或f6发动决定性的冲兵突破。实战如下：

zh: 27. Bg3 Qa4

Qg4+ Kh8 32. Qxd4 Qxc2 33. Ne1 Qd2 34. Qd7。

**Rxa2**

兵阵已冲到第六横线，清除了沿途全部障碍。

zh: 也可以通过其他方式获胜，例如 37. Qe6 或 37. Be5。

text: Qf7+ 1-0 A decisive storm of the opponent's position on the basis of a breakthrough of the pawn phalanx of e and f-pawns was also carried Out by White in the game Aronin- Flohr, (18th USSR Championship 1954).
zh:
**Qf7+ 1-0**

1950年第18届苏联锦标赛中阿罗宁对弗洛尔一局，也展示了白方以e、f兵阵突破后，向对方阵地发动的决定性进攻。〔校勘注：原书误作1954年，应为1950年。阿罗宁未参加1954年该项锦标赛，而在1950年的比赛中确曾战胜弗洛尔。〕

text: The phalanx is already deployed on the frontier, the crossing of which leads to a quick demolition of the opponent's castled position.
zh: 兵阵已抵达突破的临界位置，一旦越过，便可迅速摧毁对方易位后的阵地。

text: Black's aim is to blunt the sharp attacking march of the phalanx by exchanging queens. If， for example, 26. f6 then 26... Bxd4+ 27. Qxd4 Qb6 and the aim is achieved.
zh: 黑方希望通过兑后，削弱兵阵的攻势。例如26. f6 Bxd4+，27. Qxd4 Qb6之后，黑方便达到了兑后的目的。

zh: 26. Bxc5 Nxc5 27. Qe3 Qb6

zh: 28. Kh1 Rae8 29. f6

zh: 威胁 30. fxg7 Kxg7 31. Rf6。

text: The following encounter De Chigorin and Zukertort tween played in the international tournament at London 1883 should be considered the original game in which the strength of the pawn phalanx on the e and f-files was classically demonstrated. Admittedly, even five years before this, against Bird at the Paris tournament of 1878, Zukertort succeeded in bringing to light, in a comparatively simple form, the activity of such a phalanx.
zh: 下面这盘1883年在伦敦国际锦标赛中的齐果林对祖凯尔托特一局，可以视为经典展示e、f兵阵威力的早期范例。不过，早在五年前，祖凯尔托特就在1878年巴黎锦标赛对伯德的一局中，以相对简单的形式展现过这种兵阵的活力。

text: Spanish Game
zh: 西班牙开局

text: White: Chigorin
zh: 白方：齐果林

text: Black: Zukertort
zh: 黑方：祖凯尔托特

text: (London 1883)
1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Be7 6. d5
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Be7 6. d5

zh: 6. Re1 Nd6 7. dxe5 Nxb5 8. a4，能给黑方制造最棘手的开局问题。

text: Nd6 7. dxe5 Nxb5 8. a4. 6... Nd6! 7. Bxc6
On 7. Be2 follows 7... e4, while on 7. dxc6 Nxb5. The best continuation is 7. Nc3.
zh: 若7. Be2，则7... e4；若7. dxc6，则7... Nxb5。最好的后续手段是7. Nc3。

text: 7... dxc6 8. dxc6 f6!
zh: 7... dxc6 8. dxc6 f6!

text: And in fact the phalanx iS already mobilised. Very soon it begins its dangerous advance.
zh: 兵阵已经部署就绪，很快便将发起危险的冲击。

text: 9. cxb7 Bxb7 10. Be3 O-O 11. Nbd2 Nf7!
zh: 9. cxb7 Bxb7 10. Be3 O-O 11. Nbd2 Nf7!

text: Now, as the e5 pawn is reinforced, everything is ready for an advance of the phalanx, and it is not apparent how it can be successfully countered. All this is a result of White's 6th and 7th moves. Thus the outwardly imperceptible inaccuracies in the opening created a pre-requisite for a dangerous initiative for the opponent.
zh: e5兵得到巩固后，兵阵的前冲已准备就绪，而白方看不出有效的应对办法。这一切都源于白方第6、7步的选择。开局中看似细小的不准确，已经为黑方危险的主动权创造了条件。

text: The forcing four-move march of the pawn phalanx already yields its fruit. Now 16. gxf3 is bad in view of
zh: 兵阵连续四步强行前冲，已经取得成果。现在16. gxf3不好，因为

text: 16... Bxc5 17. Ne6 exf3 18. Qc4
zh: 16... Bxc5 17. Ne6 exf3 18. Qc4

text: Qf6 and Black remains with a material advantage, while the White king's position is totally exposed.
zh: Qf6，黑方保持子力优势，白王的位置却完全暴露。

zh: 16. Qb5 Qc8!

zh: 同时威胁...Qg4和

17. Rfd1

Qf1.

text: Qg4, on which follows 19... Nxf3! However, the White king's position, shattered by the phalanx, is so unsatisfactory that it is easy for Black to find other ways to develop the attack.
zh: Qg4，可以19. Nxf3!应对。不过，兵阵已严重破坏白王的防护，黑方很容易找到其他进攻途径。〔校勘注：原书此处写作19... Nxf3，依上下文应为白方第19步。〕

zh: 若19. Bxe7，则19... Nh3+ 20. Kh1 fxg2+等，几步后便被将杀。

zh: 现在20. Bxe7同样会遭到

zh: 最后沿白格和开放线展开的全部进攻，都以黑方f兵的行进路线...f5-f4-f3xg2为基础。白王在棋盘中心被黑子包围，已无法坚持多久。

zh: 另一种结束对局的办法是

In another classic game, the attack with the e-f pawn phalanx developed in a far more complicated situation, where a phalanx of "hanging pawns" in the centre was also operating g for the opposing side, and for some time the struggle assumed a double-edged character.
zh: 另一盘经典对局中，e、f兵阵的进攻发生在更加复杂的局面：对方中心也有悬兵兵阵，双方一度各有机会，斗争十分尖锐。

1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. e3 c5 4. b3 cxd4 4. exd4 Nc6 5. c4 Bg4 7. Be2 e6

zh: 7... dxc4 8. bxc4 Bxf3 9. Bxf3 Nxd4 10. Bxb7 Rb8 11. Bd5 e5，

zh: 显然未能令皮尔斯伯里满意，尽管我们认为黑方局面很好。不过，白方可以不用11. Bd5，而选择平稳的11. Bb2，或11.

zh: Be3，促成兑换，

text: 8. O-O dxc4
zh: 8. O-O dxc4

text: A crucial decision. "Hanging' pawns are formed for White, with all the pluses and minuses of a central 1 "hanging" phalanx. It is possible that this decision was dictated by an unwillingness to allow the move c5 with a subsequent advance of the column of White pawns on the queen's flank.
zh: 关键的决定。白方将形成中心悬兵，既有长处，也有弱点。黑方或许是不愿让白方走c5，随后让整个后翼兵群向前冲击。

text: 9. bxc4 Rc8 10. Bb2 Be7 11. Nbd2 O-O
zh: 9. bxc4 Rc8 10. Bb2 Be7 11. Nbd2 O-O

text: Upon this, the opening stage is completed. White's plan must consist of the preparation of the advance of the "hanging" phalanx, in particular with the move d5. For this, he needs in the first place to bring his rooks to the centre by Rac1 and Rfd1. Pillsbury counters this plan with an attack on the king's flank, in conjunction with pressure on the opponent's ""hanging" centre.
zh: 开局至此结束。白方应准备冲起悬兵，尤其是d5；首先要走Rac1和Rfd1，把双车调到中心。皮尔斯伯里则以王翼进攻对抗这一计划，同时向白方的悬兵中心施压。

text: 12. Qb3 Qc7 13. Rac1 Rfd8 14
zh: 12. Qb3 Qc7 13. Rac1 Rfd8 14.

text: Qe3 At least five considerations can be advanced in favour of this move: White defends the bishop e2 and thereby unpins the knight f3, he increases the pressure on the central point e5, defends the d4 pawn one more time, prevents the thrust ... Qf4, and finally takes the queen away from the threat of ... Na5. And yet the queen move merits censure, above all because it does not represent a link in the execution of the plan, outlined above, of exploiting the favourable side on the " "hanging centre. It was necessary for White to play 14. Rfd1, with the aim of playing d5! and then try to carry out the manoeuvre Nf1-e3. In any case his task is to keep the opponent under threat of a pawn a advance and thereby increase the tension in the centre as much as possible.
zh:
**Qe3**

至少有五个理由支持这步：保护e2象，解除f3马的牵制；加强对e5的控制；再保护一次d4兵；阻止...Qf4；并让后避开...Na5的攻击。尽管如此，这步动后仍值得批评，因为它没有落实利用中心悬兵长处的计划。白方应走14. Rfd1，准备d5!，再寻求Nf1-e3的运马方案。无论如何，都应让对手始终面临冲兵的威胁，尽量保持中心的紧张状态。

text: On top of everything it turns out that the position of the queen on e3 is rather bad. To prevent the threat of ... Bf4 he has to weaken the pawn cover of the castled position.
zh: 更糟的是，后在e3的位置并不好。为了防止...Bf4，白方不得不削弱易位阵地的兵屏障。

text: A "trappy" move, reckoning on
zh: 这步设下了一个陷阱，指望

text: 16... Qxa2? 17. Bc3. It is true that
White now threatens the break 17
zh: 白方现在威胁冲兵突破：17.

text: d5 exd5 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Qh6, but
zh: d5 exd5 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Qh6；但

text: this threat is parried by Black with advantage. Possibly it made sense to carry out this operation at once:
zh: 黑方能在化解这一威胁的同时取得优势。白方或许应立即行动：

text: 16. d5 exd5 17. Bxf6 gxf6 18. Qh6
zh: 16. d5 exd5 17. Bxf6 gxf6 18. Qh6

text: and 18... Be7? is not possible in view of 19. Bd3. However, after 18... Bf5 19. Qxf6 Bg6 Black retains good chances: two strong bishops firmly defend his king, while the central position is more favourable for him.
zh: 18... Be7?不行，因为19. Bd3。不过，18... Bf5 19. Qxf6 Bg6后，黑方仍有良好机会：两只强有力的象可靠地保护黑王，中心局面也对黑方有利。

text: But this already is a mistake. White does not sense the impending danger; he should return with the bishop to e2 with a subsequent
zh: 这步却是错误。白方没有察觉迫近的危险；应当退象e2，随后

text: Rfd1.
zh: Rfd1。

text: This surprising blow in the centre is only possible because of White's last move. The aim of Black's advance is to gain the f3 square.
zh: 白方上一步使这记出人意料的中心打击成为可能。黑方冲兵的目的，是夺取f3格。

text: Quite bad is 18. dxe5 Nxe5 19
zh: 18. dxe5 Nxe5 19.

text: Bxe5 Bxe5 20. Qxe5 Rxd3; both ... Rxd2 and ... h6, and ... Be2 with
zh: Bxe5 Bxe5 20. Qxe5 Rxd3很差；黑方既威胁...Rxd2、...h6，也有...Be2，

text: ... Ng4 to follow, are threatened.
zh: 随后...Ng4的威胁。

text: Black has allowed the advance of the enemy centre pawn, but has plenty of compensation in his invasion of the f3 point and likewise the possibility of advancing the e-f phalanx.
zh: 黑方虽然允许白方冲起中心兵，却能进驻f3，还可以让e、f兵阵向前冲击，补偿十分充分。

text: There is nothing better. 19. Bxd4 exd4 leads to the loss of the knight. 19. Nge4 Nxe4 20. Qxe4
zh: 白方没有更好的办法。19. Bxd4 exd4会丢马；19. Nge4 Nxe4 20. Qxe4，

text: Bf5 21. Qe2 Bxd3 22. Qxd3 Ne2+ -
zh: Bf5 21. Qe2 Bxd3 22. Qxd3 Ne2+，

text: to the loss of the exchange. 19. f3 is also unsatisfactory in view of 19... Bc5!
zh: 则会丢掉半子。19. f3也不好，因为19... Bc5!

text: 19... h6 20. Nge4 Nxe4 21. Nxe4 Nf3+ 22. Kg2 Bb8 23. Rh1
zh: 19... h6 20. Nge4 Nxe4 21. Nxe4 Nf3+ 22. Kg2 Bb8 23. Rh1

text: So as to play 24. Be2, which was impossible at once because of 23... Nxh4+. However, Black utilizes this time to activate the phalanx. An immediate 23. Nc3 was comparatively best; however, also in this case Black could play 23... f5, threatening an attack with the phalanx.
zh: 准备24. Be2。若立即走Be2，黑方就有23... Nxh4+。但黑方利用这段时间活跃兵阵。相对最好的是立即23. Nc3，不过黑方仍可23... f5，准备以兵阵发起进攻。

text: Soon there is a further advance of the phalanx, bringing with it "death 1 and destruction". White makes an attempt to provoke some activity in the centre and even manages to advance the d-pawn, but this proves inadequate for countering Black's fierce attack.
zh: 兵阵很快再次前冲，带来毁灭性的威胁。白方试图在中心反击，甚至成功冲起d兵，却仍不足以抗衡黑方的猛烈进攻。

text: The culmination of the breakthrough.
zh: 冲兵突破达到高潮。

text: 30. Kh2 Rxe5
zh: 30. Kh2 Rxe5

text: Possibly even more energetic is
zh: 或许更有力的是

zh: 威胁两步杀。f兵变成了钉子兵，完成最后的打击。

zh: 33. Bf1 Rh5

zh: 34. Rc2 Rxb5

zh: 黑方得子。若34. Qb2，则34... Bxb5，

35. Bh3 Rxh4 36. gxh4 Bxd6#。

text: Usually the phalanx breaks through the front and only then do the pieces rush into the attack. In this game it was the other way around. The attack began with the pieces, but then they had need of the pawn phalanx.
zh: 通常是兵阵先突破防线，子力再跟进。本局却恰好相反：先由子力发起进攻，再借助兵阵完成突破。

text: The attack of a pawn mass on the flanks is figuratively called a storm, but it does actually warrant this name since it develops impetuously, by force, and in the intense heat of the struggle. With castling on opposite sides, at times both opponents rush into the storm and success usually attends the one who first achieves pawn escort and begins to loosen the position of the enemy king. Not infrequently the pawn storm takes place also upon same-side castling or entirely without castling. In such cases the attacking side needs to watch closely for his own security, in voluntarily exposing his own king, and not allow the opponent to complicate the struggle by means of a counterattack.
zh: 侧翼兵群的猛烈进攻，形象地称为“兵风暴”。它来势迅猛、具有强制性，确实名副其实。异向易位时，双方有时会同时发动兵风暴，通常是谁先把兵送到对方阵地、破坏敌王的防护，谁就更容易成功。同向易位，甚至尚未易位时，也可以发动兵风暴。不过，这时进攻方主动冲起护王兵，必须格外注意自己的王，避免让对手通过反击把局面复杂化。

text: The pawn storm column usually consists of three pawns, advancing side by side on the f, g, h or a, b, c files; ; there is also a two-pawn column. The pawn storm has more chances of success if the g or h pawns in the opponent's castled position have advanced. The contact of the storming column with such pawns takes place two tempi earlier than with pawns on their original squares, and as a consequence the general tempo of attack is apparently accelerated.
zh: 兵风暴通常由f、g、h三兵，或a、b、c三兵并列前冲，也可以只由两个兵组成。如果对方易位阵地的g兵或h兵已经冲起，兵风暴就更容易奏效：与这些兵接触，比它们仍在原始格时要快两个先手，整个进攻速度也就明显加快。

text: It is necessary to carefully calculate a pawn storm. However, this is a far from easy task. In the majority of cases a certain amount of risk is involved in the storm. Even when the pawn column achieves the aim and comes into contact with the opponent's pawns, one has to weigh up the character of the piece battle which must develop after the disappearance of pawns from the battle zone. It must not be forgotten that the advance of the pawn group creates various positional weaknesses in the rear, and if the storm does not succeed then things might surprisingly turn out to be "no better off than at the start". Let us give some illustrations.
zh: 发动兵风暴需要仔细计算，而这并不容易，往往必须承担一定风险。即使兵群已抵达目标并与对方兵接触，还要判断兑兵、打开战区之后的子力战斗。兵群前冲也会在己方后方留下弱点；如果进攻未能奏效，最后可能发现局面并不比最初更好。下面看几个例子。

text: In Vidmar-Tarrasch (Nurnberg 1906) White begins a pawn storm on the king's flank. The basis for this is the weakening of Black's castled position by the move ... h6 and the cramped position of his bishop on f6. He can do nothing in the centre and this makes the flank attack safe.
zh: 1906年在纽伦堡的维德马尔对塔拉什一局中，白方开始发动王翼兵风暴。依据是黑方走过...h6，易位阵地有所削弱，而且f6象活动受限。黑方在中心无从反击，使白方的侧翼进攻较为安全。

text: 18... Nxe3 is inadequate in view of 19. Qxe3 when White threatens Nxf6+ followed by
zh: 18... Nxe3不足以解决问题，因为19. Qxe3，白方威胁Nxf6+后

text: Qxh6. If 19... Kh7, then 20. h4. 19. h4 Ng8 20. g5
If Black's pawn were still on h7, this move would not have the same strength it acquires now.
zh: 如果黑方h兵仍在h7，这步就不会有现在这样大的威力。

text: 20... hxg5 21. hxg5 Be7 22. Ne5
zh: 20... hxg5 21. hxg5 Be7 22. Ne5

text: The storm yields its fruit. The Black king's position has appreciably deteriorated, his knight has been pushed back to g8 and does not have a single move, the f7 and g7 points are weak. White's pieces, on the other hand, are very actively placed, the open h-file can be occupied without difficulty, and also a concrete plan begins to show for the realisation of the positional advantage, for example Bd2 followed by Qf3.
zh: 兵风暴已经见效。黑王的处境明显恶化，马被赶回g8，无处可去，f7和g7也很薄弱。白方子力却十分活跃，可以轻松占据开放的h线，并已有兑现局面优势的具体计划，例如Bd2后Qf3。

text: In the event of 22... g6 23. Bd2, the threat of Qf3 is irresistible.
zh: 若22... g6 23. Bd2，Qf3的威胁无法化解。

text: 23. Ng6+ Kf7 24. Nh8+ Ke8 25. Nc5 f5 26. Qe2 g6 27. Nxg6 and
Black soon resigned.
zh: 黑方很快认输。

text: Let us look at a few games. The peculiarity of the first of these lies in the fact that White begins a pawn storm on the king's flank even before Black has castled, almost in the opening stage, and in the present case, together with a particular aim - to open the position of the king, it has also the object of preventing Black from castling on the king's side. To place the king under frontal attack from the infantry would, on his part, be foolhardy.
zh: 下面再看几盘完整对局。第一局的特点是，白方几乎在开局阶段、黑方尚未易位时，就发动王翼兵风暴。除了暴露黑王的位置，还意在阻止黑方短易位：把王放到迎面而来的兵群之前，显然太冒险。

text: Hungarian Defence
zh: 匈牙利防御

text: White: A.Alekhine
zh: 白方：A.阿廖欣

text: Black: G.Breyer
zh: 黑方：G.布雷耶尔

text: (Mannheim 1914)
1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d4 d6 5. Nc3 Bg4 6. h3 Bxf3
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d4 d6 5. Nc3 Bg4 6. h3 Bxf3

text: The aim of this exchanging operation, in conjunction with the following move, lies in the fact that it obliges White to close the centre. And, in fact, he has to "lock up" the centre without delay and set about enlivening the situation on the flank.
zh: 这次兑换结合下一步，意在迫使白方封闭中心。白方确实必须立即锁住中心，再到侧翼寻找积极行动。

text: 7. Qxf3 Nf6 8. d5 Nb8
zh: 7. Qxf3 Nf6 8. d5 Nb8

text: Clearly, not 8... Nd4 9. Qd3 and then Be3 when the knight already needs to retreat, but has nowhere to go!
zh: 显然不能8... Nd4，因为9. Qd3后Be3，黑马必须退，却无处可退！

text: 9. Be3 Nbd7 10. g4
zh: 9. Be3 Nbd7 10. g4

text: As is seen from the further course of the game, this thrust introduces a general pawn storm on the king's flank.
zh: 后续实战表明，这步是全面发动王翼兵风暴的开端。

text: A dubious move. Black will now be very cramped, and the knight, from f6, has to go to g8, where it is both locked in itself, and also locks in the rook. He should play 11... N6d7, preparing a pawn storm on the queen's flank in the event of White's castling on that side.
zh: 可疑的一步。黑方将陷入拥挤局面，f6马必须退到g8，既困住自己，又堵住车。黑方应走11... N6d7，准备在白方长易位后发动后翼兵风暴。

text: 12. Bb5 c6 13. Be2 Bd8
zh: 12. Bb5 c6 13. Be2 Bd8

text: In the quest for operational space for his pieces. More unpleasant for White would be the reply 13... a6 with the threat ... c5 and a future enlivening of his pawns on the queen's flank. If 14. g5 Ng8 15. Na4, then already good is 15. Bd8, retaining the possibility of playing ... c5 and possibly also ... b5.
zh: 黑方试图为子力寻找活动空间。13... a6能给白方更多麻烦，准备...c5，并活跃后翼兵群。若14. g5 Ng8 15. Na4，则15... Bd8很好，保留了...c5乃至...b5的可能。

text: Bxb6
zh: Bxb6

text: White is carried away with the storm and goes for the exchange, after which he succeeds in forcibly carrying out f4 and adding the f-pawn to the attacking column of the h and g-pawns.
zh: 白方一心发动兵风暴，选择兑换，借此强制实现f4，把f兵加入h兵、g兵组成的进攻兵群。

text: The storm is in full swing, but Black has managed to transfer one of his inactive knights to the weak f4 square, while he has in prospect the possibility of castling on the queen's side, that is to take his king out of the zone of attack. Perhaps he still need not despair!
zh: 兵风暴正在猛烈展开，但黑方已把一匹原本不活跃的马调到f4弱格，还可能长易位，让王离开攻击区域。黑方也许还不必绝望。

text: A sharp and risky attempt to counter the column storming its way to the king's position. A pawn battle now flares up at once. The position is so complicated and unusual that it is difficult to suggest any kind of clear defensive plan. Possibly 20... Nxe2+ 21. Qxe2
zh: 黑方尖锐而冒险地迎击冲向王的兵群，兵的战斗立即爆发。局面复杂而罕见，很难提出清晰的防守计划。或许可走20... Nxe2+ 21. Qxe2，

text: O-O-O 22. Rh3 Kb8 23. Qc4 (If 23. Rd3, then 23... Ne7, and then ...
Nc8, and the b6 and d6 squares are reliably defended) 23 3... h6 24
zh: Nc8，b6和d6便得到可靠保护）23... h6 24.

text: dxc5 bxc5 25. gxh6 Rxh6 etc.
zh: dxc6 bxc6 25. gxh6 Rxh6等。〔校勘注：原书此处误作24. dxc5 bxc5；按局面应在c6兑换。〕

text: White retains attacking possibilities by playing a further a4 and b4, but all the same there is quite a lot of potential resistance remaining for Black. Breyer, apparently, decides to keep a firm hold on his cavalry outpost. In this, clearly, lies the point of the text move.
zh: 白方仍可继续a4、b4争取进攻，但黑方也有相当多的抵抗资源。布雷耶尔显然决定保住马的前哨据点，这就是实战这步的用意。

text: Without mentioning the fact that this move is a direct mistake (admittedly, not exploited by White), nothing can justify the journey of the king into the storm region. This may be courageous, but also reckless!
zh: 且不说这步是直接的错误——白方也没有抓住——把王送进兵风暴的攻击区域，本身就毫无道理。勇气可嘉，却太鲁莽！

text: Black could not take the pawn twice: 22... fxg6 23. hxg6 Nxg6 in view of the pin 24. Bh5. Castling is also unfavourable - 22... O-O-O 23
zh: 黑方不能连续吃兵：22... fxg6 23. hxg6 Nxg6，因为24. Bh5形成牵制。长易位也不利：22... O-O-O 23.

text: gxf7 Nxe2+ 24. Nxe2 Ne7 25. Rhf1 f5 26. dxc6 bxc6 27. exf5 Nd5 28
zh: gxf7 Nxe2+ 24. Nxe2 Ne7 25. Rhf1 f5 26. dxc6 bxc6 27. exf5 Nd5 28.

text: Qa3. However, by continuing 22
zh: Qa3。不过，若改走22...

text: ... fxg6 23. hxg6 and only now 23
zh: fxg6 23. hxg6，再走23...

text: O-O-O, Black, with an extra pawn, can rightfully look forward to the future with confidence. In any event, there would still be a very stubborn struggle in prospect.
zh: O-O-O，黑方多一兵，可以对前景抱有信心。至少，双方还有漫长而顽强的斗争。

text: 23. gxf7
zh: 23. gxf7

text: Carried away with his plan to expose the position of the enemy king, White does not notice a surprising new possibility which has presented itself - to win at least a knight by 23. g7+! Kxg7 24. Rhg1+ and the knight must cover, since 24... Kf8 (or 24... Kh7) would lead to an even more deplorable result after 25. Qg3.
zh: 白方一心剥去黑王的掩护，却漏掉了一个出人意料的新机会：23. g7+! Kxg7 24. Rhg1+，至少可以得马。黑方必须用马挡将，因为24... Kf8或24... Kh7都会遭到25. Qg3，后果更糟。

text: Now Black takes heart and the struggle once again assumes a quite fierce character.
zh: 黑方重新振作，斗争再次变得十分激烈。

text: 23... Ne7 24. Bg4 cxd5 25. exd5 f5 26. Bf3 Qc5 27. Qe1 Kxf7
zh: 23... Ne7 24. Bg4 cxd5 25. exd5 f5 26. Bf3 Qc5 27. Qe1 Kxf7

text: And so Black, as before, has an extra pawn, his pieces occupy good positions on the queen's flank, and he has two operation-files - "a" and "c". All would be well, if it were still possible ... to ensure the safety of his king, but it is just this which is difficult, and possibly even an insoluble problem. White's plan of attack consists of an exchange sacrifice on f4 and an invasion on the e-file.
zh: 黑方仍多一兵，子力在后翼位置良好，又掌握a线和c线两条活动线路。只要能确保王的安全，局面本来很不错；可这恰恰是最困难、甚至可能无解的问题。白方准备在f4弃半子，再沿e线侵入。

text: 28. Rh4 Ke8 29. Kb1
zh: 28. Rh4 Ke8 29. Kb1

text: So as, after 30. Rxf4 exf4, to not be threatened with an exchange of queens.
zh: 准备在30. Rxf4 exf4之后，避免黑方提出兑后。

text: He should play 29... Rh7 or 29
Rg8 (with the aim, after 30
zh: Rg8，准备在30.

text: Rxf4 exf4 31. Qe6, to have the move Rg1). Also 29... Rc8 is
zh: Rxf4 exf4 31. Qe6之后用...Rg1应对。29... Rc8也

text: worthy of attention.
zh: 值得关注。

text: 30. Rxf4 exf4 31. Qe6 Kd8
zh: 30. Rxf4 exf4 31. Qe6 Kd8

text: There is much that Black does not foresee, but even on the best defence, 31... Rc8, it would be difficult to save the game. Interesting variations are obtained: 31 .
zh: 黑方漏算了很多，但即使采用最好的防守31... Rc8，也很难救回局面。下面的变化颇有意思：31...

text: Rc8 32. Be2 b4 33. Bb5+ Kf8 34. Qf6+ Kg8 35. Bd7 and wins, or 32... Rc7 33. Bxb5+ Kd8 34. Re1 Qb6 (34... Rh7 35. Qg8+) 35. a4 Qc5 36. Qf6 Rg8 37. Qf7 Rh8 38. Qg7 Rg8 39. Qxg8+ and Re8 mate. 32. Nxb5! Qxb5
zh:
Rc8 32. Be2 b4 33. Bb5+ Kf8 34. Qf6+ Kg8 35. Bd7，白方胜；或32... Rc7 33. Bxb5+ Kd8 34. Re1 Qb6（34... Rh7 35. Qg8+）35. a4 Qc5 36. Qf6 Rg8 37. Qf7 Rh8 38. Qg7 Rg8 39. Qxg8+，随后Re8#。

**32. Nxb5! Qxb5**

text: Black is already a rook up, but not for long.
zh: 黑方已多一车，但这只是暂时的。

text: 33. Qxd6+ Qd7 Or 33... Ke8 34. Re1 Qd7 35. Qg6+ Kd8 36. Qf6 Rg8 37. d6. 34. Qf6 Rh7 35. d6 Ke8 36. Re1 Ra6 37. Qg6+ Rf7 38. Bd5 Rxd6 39. Qxf7 + Kd8 40. Qf8+ Qe8 41. Qxe8+ Kxe8 42. Bxb7
The White pawns advance irrepressably. Black resigned on the 51st move.
zh: 白方的兵锐不可当。黑方第51步认输。

text: Sicilian Defence
zh: 西西里防御

text: White: : G.Kasparyan
zh: 白方：G.卡斯帕里扬

text: Black: G.Levenfish
zh: 黑方：G.列文菲什

text: (10th USSR Championship 1937)
zh: （1937年第10届苏联锦标赛）

text: 1. e4 c5 2. Ne2 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Bg5 e6 7. Qd2 Be7 8. O-O-O O-O
zh: 1. e4 c5 2. Ne2 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Bg5 e6 7. Qd2 Be7 8. O-O-O O-O

text: The opposite-side castling, characteristic for this variation of the Sicilian Defence, predetermines White's plan, which consists of the carrying out of a pawn storm on the king's flank. Not without foundation there is an opinion that there is no need for Black to hurry with the removal of his king to the flank, and in a number of games he carries out castling after a preliminary 8... Nxd4 9. Qxd4, and if 10. f4, then 10... Qa5. Admittedly, also in this case prospects of a pawn attack on the king's position remain for White.
zh: 这一西西里防御变化常形成异向易位，白方的计划也因此明确：在王翼发动兵风暴。有一种颇有道理的看法，认为黑方不必急于易位，可以先8... Nxd4 9. Qxd4，再易位；若10. f4，则10... Qa5。不过，即使如此，白方仍有用兵进攻黑王的机会。

text: 9. f4 Qa5
zh: 9. f4 Qa5

text: On 9... h6 White replies 10. h4. Deserving attention is 9... e5 - an idea advanced by Geller and successfully tested in several games - which has the aim of making it difficult for White to organise a storm.
zh: 若9... h6，白方应以10. h4。盖勒提出的9... e5值得重视，它在数盘对局中成功经受了检验，目的是增加白方组织兵风暴的难度。

text: The move in the game is not quite satisfactory. In any case, if such a development of the queen is planned then he should first of all exchange on d4.
zh: 实战这步不够好。即使准备这样出后，黑方也应先在d4兑换。

text: 10. Nb3 Qb6 11. Be2 Rd8 12. g4 Bd7 13. f5 Ne5 14. h4 Rac8 15. Bxf6 Bxf6 16. g5 Be7 17. h5
zh: 10. Nb3 Qb6 11. Be2 Rd8 12. g4 Bd7 13. f5 Ne5 14. h4 Rac8 15. Bxf6 Bxf6 16. g5 Be7 17. h5

text: A colourful picture of a storm. Black is excellently mobilised, his knight is placed in the centre of the board on a weak square, both his rooks operate in the direction of the centre, one of them is located on the open c-file which leads straight to the haven of the enemy king. However, White is also attacking with his three-pawn storm-group, and this is his only, but very important, positional plus. With the next moves, his pawns enter into contact with the Black king's defensive cover, bring about necessary exchanges, and then White's piece army, in the first instance his queen and rook, begin to operate very powerfully against the breach which has been created on the file.
zh: 这是兵风暴进攻的一幅生动画面。黑方出子充分，马占据中心弱格，双车都作用于中心，其中一车还占据直接通向白王的开放c线。白方的优势则在于三兵组成的进攻群，虽然只有这一点，却十分重要。接下来，白兵将与黑王的护卫兵接触，进行必要的兑换，再由后、车等子力沿打开的线路强力进攻。

text: Clearly, not 17... exf5 in view of 18. Nd5.
zh: 显然不能17... exf5，因为18. Nd5。

text: 18. Rdf1 d5
zh: 18. Rdf1 d5

text: Correct tactics! A flank attack is best met by an attack in the centre. Black sacrifices a pawn (19. fxe6 fxe6 20. exd5) but White does not consider accepting the "Greek" gift at the cost of giving up the storm and handing over the initiative to the opponent (20... Bb4).
zh: 正确的应对！对侧翼进攻，最好用中心反击来对抗。黑方弃兵：19. fxe6 fxe6 20. exd5，但白方不愿为接受这份诱人的“礼物”而中断兵风暴，并在20... Bb4后把主动权交给黑方。

text: 19. g6 dxe4
zh: 19. g6 dxe4

text: Black consistently opens the centre, where all his pieces sare operating. The variation 19
zh: 黑方贯彻原来的构想，打开全部子力正在发挥作用的中心。例如以下变化：19...

text: fxg6 20. hxg6 h6 21. Nxd5 exd5 22. Qxd5+ Be6! 23. Qxe6+ Qxe6 24
zh: fxg6 20. hxg6 h6 21. Nxd5 exd5 22. Qxd5+ Be6! 23. Qxe6+ Qxe6 24.

text: fxe6 relieves the crisis rather in White's favour (24... Nxg6 25. Rf7), though it was acceptable for Black.
zh: fxe6，局势趋于缓和，白方较为有利（24... Nxg6 25. Rf7），不过黑方仍可以接受。

text: Worse is 22. fxg7+ Bxg7 and now 23. Qe1 is not possible because of 23... f5!. Now, however, he threatens to take on g7 and then play h6 and Qh4. The reply is therefore forced.
zh: 22. fxg7+ Bxg7更差，因为23. Qe1会遭到23... f5!。实战这步则威胁在g7吃兵，再走h6和Qh4，因此黑方的应手是被迫的。

text: The storm yields its fruit - the
zh: 兵风暴已经奏效：

text: Black king's position is exposed. The main artery for a piece attack is the g-file and to a certain extent also the f-file.
zh: 黑王的位置暴露。子力进攻的主要通道是g线，f线也能发挥一定作用。

text: Though Black has purposefully exploited the time which White has spent on the storm (he has opened and seized the centre and worsened the position of the enemy king), White's attack is nevertheless the more dangerous.

text: With this we conclude our look at the theme about pawns as an attacking force. It remains to note that, despite the extensive amount of material presented in this chapter and partly also in other sections of the book, the question about the active role of pawns in no way can be considered as exhausted. We came across it once again in the final chapters and particularly in the second part of the work, where we give special consideration to the combinational role of pawns.
zh: 本章关于兵作为进攻力量的讨论到此结束。虽然本章及其他章节提供了许多例子，但兵的积极作用远未讨论完。后面的章节，尤其是本书第二部分，还会再次涉及这一问题，并专门讨论兵在战术组合中的作用。

text: The Struggle with Heavy Pieces
zh: 重子斗争

text: In the introduction we have already pointed out the presence of a highly significant difference e between the middlegame and endgame stages. The transition into the endgame to a considerable extent changes both the whole thematic struggle, which means also the planning of it, and methods of operation. It is very important to mention that in t the endgame the evaluation of weak and strong points is changed and also the significance of open lines, the role of theory and technique increases, and particular requirements for handling pawns arise.
zh: 导言中已经指出，中局与残局有着十分重要的区别。转入残局后，斗争的主题、计划和行动方法都会发生很大变化。尤其需要注意的是，强点、弱点以及开放线的意义都会随之改变，理论知识和技术的重要性上升，运用兵也有了特殊要求。

text: In this connection the question inevitably arises: to what extent in the central stage of the game is it necessary to be guided by considerations coming out of the possibility of transferring the struggle to the endgame? You see the game of chess presents itself as a single whole and, despite the significant difference in the positional requirements of the middlegame and endgame, never should it be forgotten that in many cases even the most sharp and tense struggle in the middlegame receives its completion deep in the endgame.
zh: 由此自然产生一个问题：在中局阶段，应当在多大程度上考虑将来转入残局的可能性？一盘棋毕竟是一个整体。尽管中局和残局对局面的要求差别很大，我们仍须记住，许多激烈而紧张的中局斗争，要到残局深处才能分出胜负。

text: It is possible to reply to this question in a general way, that, taking into account the possibility of the future endgame, one should not exaggerate its role and so much the more attach decisive importance to the solving of the creative problems of the middlegame and even some openings.
zh: 一般说来，应当考虑未来可能出现的残局，但不能夸大这一因素的作用，更不能让它决定中局、甚至某些开局阶段的构思。

text: Let us say there is no need to worsen one's pawn formation in vain, since this might have an unfavourable effect in the endgame. But if a concrete plan of action, intended in the middlegame, requires the creation of backward, doubled, isolated and even a formation of pawns, then it is necessary to go in for this by discarding abstract considerations, relevent only to the endgame.
zh: 例如，不应无端破坏自己的兵形，因为这可能在残局中带来不利影响。但若中局的具体行动计划要求承担落后兵、叠兵、孤兵等兵形弱点，就应当接受，抛开那些仅适用于残局的抽象顾虑。

text: It is well-known, for example, that Lasker,by（ choosing the exchange variation of the Spanish Game as White (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6), was planning, after 4... dxc6, to exploit the extra pawn on the king's flank in the endgame. He carried out this plan with success in match games against Janowski i and Tarrasch. This did not prevent Lasker, in the international tourmnament at Nirnberg 1896, finishing off Tarrasch in the same variation even before the transfer of the game into an ending. A still more striking example was the game Lasker-Capablanca (Petersburg 1914). Capablanca, familiar with Lasker's planned line to the endgame, in the exchange variation, blockaded the e-pawn and planned an attack on it with the rooks on the open e-file together with support from the bishop on b7. The struggle developed in the middlegame, in which Lasker did not stop at the advance f5, as a result of which the e4 pawn became backward and weak. At the decisive moment of the struggle he sacrificed this pawn, to invade with the knight on the sixth rank and the rooks on the seventh, and literally smashed his dangerous opponent. In conceiving the idea of attack, Lasker assessed his prospects finely and deeply and disregarded considerations about a possible endgame.
zh: 例如，众所周知，拉斯克执白采用西班牙开局兑换变例（1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6），计划在4... dxc6之后利用残局中王翼多兵的优势。他在对雅诺夫斯基和塔拉什的对抗赛中成功执行了这一计划。不过，在1896年纽伦堡国际大赛上，他用同一变例甚至在进入残局之前就击败了塔拉什。更鲜明的例子是1914年彼得堡的拉斯克对卡帕布兰卡一局。卡帕布兰卡熟悉拉斯克转入残局的计划，于是在兑换变例中封锁e兵，准备用e线双车并由b7象支援来攻击它。战斗仍在中局展开，拉斯克毫不犹豫地冲起f5，使e4兵成为落后弱兵。在斗争的决定性时刻，他又弃掉这个兵，让马侵入第六横线、双车叠入第七横线，彻底击溃了这位强劲的对手。拉斯克在构思进攻时，对自己的前景作出了细致而深入的判断，完全没有受可能转入残局这一因素的束缚。

text: In short, if it is possible to combine the positional requirements of the middlegame and endgame - so much the better. But if they clash, then preference must be given to the requirements of the middlegame.
zh: 如果能兼顾中局和残局的要求，自然最好；若两者发生冲突，则应优先满足中局的需要。

text: These questions arise in a particularly sharp fashion in positions where only queens and rooks on each side take part in the struggle (obviously, besides the pawns). The feature of this sort of middlegame position consists of the fact that the exchange of one of the pieces leads to an endgame - a queen or a rook. Here, calculation of the endgame situation becomes one of the most important factors for assessment.
zh: 当双方除兵以外，只剩后和车参加斗争时，这个问题尤其突出。这类中局的特点是，只需兑掉一对棋子，就会转入后残局或车残局。因此，对可能出现的残局作出判断，便成为评价当前局面的重要依据之一。

text: In chess literature the opinion is expressed that it is necessary to treat positions with heavy piece material as an endgame. This is a profound error.
zh: 有些国际象棋著作主张，应把只剩重子的局面当作残局处理。这是根本性的错误。

text: A characteristic feature of the concluding stage of the game is the full right of the king to take part in the struggle. The king in the endgame is an active piece, which frequently decides the outcome of the battle. Meanwhile, in the presence of the queen and rook, the king is obliged to seek shelter behind pawn cover, and forgetting this truth prompted by the mistaken notion that the struggle has proceeded to the endgame, might end and actually does end in a very sad way.
zh: 残局的一个典型特点，是王能够充分参加战斗，成为活跃的棋子，并常常决定胜负。但当双方仍有后和车时，王必须躲在兵的掩护之下。如果误以为已经进入残局，忘记了这一点，就很可能付出惨重的代价；实战中这样的例子并不少见。

text: At the same time the king must be ready to rush immediately into battle the moment the queens are exchanged and a rook ending ensues. On the other hand, in positions where an exchange of one of the heavy pieces leads to the endgame phase, great attention has to be paid to the pawn formation, to see that it is as comfortable as possible for the end-stage. The presence of passed pawns is of particular significance. Often this advantage acquires a decisive character. You see it is necessary to bring to a halt the advance of a passed pawn, in the present case the role of a blockading piece is not appropriate for the king, while to waste the energy of a queen or rook on the blockade of a pawn means conceding an advantage in force to the opponent for the rest of the struggle.
zh: 与此同时，王又必须随时准备在兑后转入车残局后立即参战。另一方面，既然兑掉一对重子就可能进入残局，便应特别注意兵形，尽量使它适合残局。通路兵在这里尤为重要，往往能成为决定性的优势。对手必须阻止它前进，但在当前局面中，王不宜承担封锁任务；若用后或车封锁兵，又会牵制这枚重子的力量，让对手在其他战场形成兵力优势。

text: The features of the struggle, inherent in this individual phase of the middlegame, also make up the contents of the present chapter.
zh: 本章讨论的，就是这一特殊中局阶段的斗争特点。

text: Here we have a position from the 5th match game Schlechter- Lasker (1910).
zh: 图中局面出自1910年施莱希特对拉斯克对抗赛的第五局。

text: Can it be contended that either one of the sides has the advantage? Of course not. More than this, many chessplayers would shake hands and go away peacefully.
zh: 能说哪一方占优吗？当然不能。甚至可以说，许多棋手在这里就会握手言和。

text: On the board we are on the verge of an endgame, but this verge will last for many moves and will not be crossed.
zh: 局面已接近残局，但接下来的许多步，双方都会停留在这一边界上，并不真正进入残局。

text: In such positions, the loss of a pawn is tantamount to defeat; on the other hand the weakening of the b6 point plays no role at all.
zh: 在这样的局面中，丢掉一兵就等于输棋；反之，b6格被削弱却无关紧要。

text: He is not afraid of weakening the d4 point, which could prove dangerous if minor pieces were taking part in the S struggle. However, for an endgame position, the pawn is better left on c2. The weakness of the Black pawn on d6 is imaginary.
zh: 白方不怕削弱d4格；只有在轻子仍参加战斗时，这个弱点才可能带来危险。不过，若从残局的角度考虑，c兵最好留在c2。黑方的d6兵也只是表面上显得薄弱。

text: Lasker carefully, via the rear of communications, brings his king nearer to the c centre and the queen's flank. For the endgame, the king of course is best situated alongside his main group of pawns, which is the only place where it can assume an offensive. Black thereby begins to carry out a plan of enlivening the play on the queen's flank. At the same time a particular problem is also solved transfer of the function of defence of the d6 pawn to the king, which frees the queen from this role. The king is clearly more securely placed
zh: 拉斯克谨慎地让王沿己方后排向中心和后翼靠拢。从残局的角度看，王最好靠近自己的主要兵群，因为只有在那里才有进攻的可能。黑方开始执行活跃后翼局面的计划，同时解决了一个具体问题：让王接替保护d6兵的任务，把后解放出来。

text: on g8 or f8 than on c7, but even here it is difficult to get near it, There are not many pieces on the board, while Black's pawn chain on the queen's flank is quite solid.
zh: 王在g8或f8当然比在c7更安全，不过即使在c7，对手也很难接近它：棋盘上子力不多，而黑方后翼兵链相当稳固。

text: White has ventured a sort of pawn storm, intending to create some threats to the Black king. Passive play is not to Lasker's taste and he boldly accepts the challenge.
zh: 白方冒险发动兵风暴，准备威胁黑王。拉斯克不愿被动应付，勇敢地接受了挑战。

text: Possibly a little risky, but a move which is full of initiative that poses White a serious problem. Black strives for a position in which an exchange of queens will be favourable for him. This allows him to achieve great freedom of activity in so far as White has to avoid the endgame. The negative side to the move is the rather weakened pawn cover of his king. Meanwhile it is still a long way to the endgame, indeed will he even succeed in achieving it.
zh: 这步或许有些冒险，却积极争取主动，给白方出了难题。黑方力求形成兑后对自己有利的局面，使白方必须回避残局，从而为自己争取更大的活动自由。不过，这步也明显削弱了黑王的兵屏障。眼下离残局还远，究竟能否顺利转入残局，还是个问题。

text: 32. cxb5

Obviously Schlechter intended proving to his mighty opponent that on the board the middlegame still rules. However, White also must be wary. In n view of the weakness of the a3 pawn and the possibility of the break ... c5, the rook ending is totally unacceptable for him. Besides this, the minus of the move h3, made earlier instead of g3, becomes clear. Because of this natural and, on the face of it, best continuation, 32. Qd3 proves to be impossible in view of 32... Qa1+ 33. Kh2 Qa2! 34. c5 dxc5 35. bxc5 Rd7 36. Qc3 Qd2! 37. Qe5+ Kb7, and the extra pawn on the queen's flank and control of the d-file gives White real chances of victory.
zh: 施莱希特显然想向这位强劲的对手证明，眼下仍是中局。但白方自己也须谨慎：a3兵薄弱，加上黑方可能以... c5冲兵突破，车残局对白方完全不能接受。此前走h3而非g3的弊端也开始显现。正因如此，看起来自然且最好的后续手段32. Qd3不能成立，因为32... Qa1+ 33. Kh2 Qa2! 34. c5 dxc5 35. bxc5 Rd7 36. Qc3 Qd2! 37. Qe5+ Kb7，黑方凭借后翼多兵和对d线的控制，获得切实的胜机。〔校勘注：原书写作“白方”，与所列变化及上下文矛盾；此处按“黑方”理解。〕

text: With the aim of avoiding variations, analogous to that cited in the previous note, and likewise guaranteeing a post nearer to the centre for the king. Now, however, the h3 3 pawn is weakened. It is interesting that Schlechter, a brilliant representative of the Vienna school, in the creative work of which the exploitation of positional weaknesses was achieved with filigree technique, nevertheless decides on this.
zh: 这步既是为了避免上一条注解所列的那类变化，也为王准备了一个更靠近中心的位置。不过，h3兵因此变弱。施莱希特是维也纳学派的杰出代表，擅长以精细的技术利用局面弱点；即使如此，他仍决定主动接受这个弱点，颇值得注意。

text: Now the rook can be transferred in the shortest time for play on both flanks. It also prepares a demonstration against the h3 pawn. The position is appreciably sharpened.
zh: 现在车可以迅速转往任一侧翼，也准备向h3兵施压。局面明显变得尖锐。

text: White e likewise exploits his chance excellently. He eprepares the move a4, as a result of which the position of the enemy king becomes even more uneasy. 35. Qa2, with the same aim, was worse in view of the reply 35... Qe6.
zh: 白方也出色地利用了自己的机会。他准备冲起a4，使黑王更加不安。同样为了这一目的，35. Qa2却较差，因为黑方可应以35... Qe6。

text: A fine reply to White's threat. In the event of 36. a4 could follow 36... bxa4 37. Qxa4 Kb7 38. Ra3 Qxe4+ 39. Kh2 Qd4! 40. Qa6+ Kc7 41. Qa7+ Qxa7 42. Rxa7+ Kb6. Now Lasker's move is clear: the f-pawn is removed from attack. And after 43. Rxg7 Re4 Black must win the endgame.
zh: 这是应对白方威胁的好办法。若36. a4，则可能出现36... bxa4 37. Qxa4 Kb7 38. Ra3 Qxe4+ 39. Kh2 Qd4! 40. Qa6+ Kc7 41. Qa7+ Qxa7 42. Rxa7+ Kb6。现在拉斯克这步的用意便清楚了：让f兵避开攻击。43. Rxg7 Re4之后，黑方应能赢下残局。

text: Schlechter does not fall into the finely woven spider's web, r recognising that his chances can only be in the middlegame.
zh: 施莱希特没有落入这张精心编织的网。他清楚，自己的机会只存在于中局。

text: It seems that Schlechter consiously provokes his opponent in all the future play, in which he counts on finding a convenient moment for a4.
zh: 施莱希特接下来似乎一直在有意引诱对手，等待适当时机冲起a4。

text: White goes in for a new weakening of the position, refraining from 38. Qg4, and he is absolutely right. Anything but an endgame!
zh: 白方放弃38. Qg4，宁愿再给自己的局面添一个弱点。这一判断完全正确：无论如何都不能转入残局！

text: A presumptuous invasion of the queen. Undoubtedly he should continue 38... Ra8, in order to radically do away with White's main and perhaps only chance, consisting C of the advance of the a-pawn. It is possible that Lasker, not seeing a clear way to further strengthen his position, in his turn decides to provoke Schlechter into the following bayonet attack, placing his hopes on the fact that this is associated with material sacrifices.
zh: 后深入得过于冒进。黑方无疑应走38... Ra8，彻底消除白方冲起a兵这一主要、甚至可能是唯一的机会。也许拉斯克看不出继续加强局面的明确办法，便反过来引诱施莱希特发动接下来的兵的攻击，指望白方为此弃掉子力。

text: White might not get another opportunity. Soon Black will be convinced that it is not so easy to defend his king even against the comparatively small 1 numbers of attacking forces.
zh: 白方可能不会再有这样的机会。黑方很快就会发现，即使进攻子力不多，保卫自己的王也绝非易事。

text: No worse is 39... Ra8 40. axb5 Qxb5 41. Qb3 Ra1! 42. Rd3 Kb6 and if 43. Rxd6 then 43... Qf1+ 44. Kg3 Qg1+ and wins. However, Lasker is in a hurry to make material gains, the more so that there are no apparent immediate dangers for the king.
zh: 39... Ra8也不差：40. axb5 Qxb5 41. Qb3 Ra1! 42. Rd3 Kb6，若43. Rxd6，则43... Qf1+ 44. Kg3 Qg1+，黑方胜。不过，拉斯克急于取得子力优势，尤其是因为当时看不出王会立即遭遇危险。

text: 40. axb5 Qxb5
zh: **40. axb5 Qxb5**

text: And so Black has won a pawn. But has White anything in return and in general? Undoubtedly yes. The enemy king's pawn cover is loosened still further, files sare opened which are aimed directly at its position. White threatens to take the initiative.
zh: 黑方得了一兵，但白方是否有补偿？无疑有。黑王的兵屏障进一步松动，直接通向黑王所在区域的线也打开了。白方已经有夺取主动权的威胁。

text: 41. Rb3 Qa6 42. Qd4
With the aim of playing Qb4, and then Ra3.
zh: 准备走Qb4，随后Ra3。

text: Black introduces the rook into the defence via the e5 square.
zh: 黑方准备让车经e5转入防守。

text: 43. Rb1 Re5 44. Qb4 Qb5
On 44... Rb5 follows 45. Qc4.
45. Qe1 Qd3 46. Rb4
Not only defending, but also threatening t the strong attacking move Qa1. Here real threats to the king also emerge for White.
zh: 这步兼顾防守，并制造了以Qa1强力进攻的威胁。白王现在也开始面临实质性的危险。

text: Black himself exposes still further the position of his own king, obviously confident that he has reliable defensive resources and wishing to realise his material advantage more quickly. The move 46... Rb5 is repulsed by the reply 47. Ra4 and if 47... Rb1 then 48. Qa5+ Kd7 49. Qf5+.
zh: 黑方主动进一步暴露自己的王，显然相信防守可靠，并希望尽快兑现子力优势。若46... Rb5，白方可用47. Ra4反击；若47... Rb1，则48. Qa5+ Kd7 49. Qf5+。

text: Commentators of this difficult game considered the best defence to be 46... Ra5 with the threat ... Ra3. However, the queen ending obtained after 47. Rb3 Qxb3 48 Qxa5+ Kb7 49. Qd8 Qe6 50. f3 d5 51. exd5 cxd5 52. Qa5 Qd7 53 Qb4+ Kc7 54. Qd4 is not entirely simple and it is not clear whether Black can win it.
zh: 评注这盘复杂对局的棋手认为，最好的防守是46... Ra5，威胁... Ra3。不过，在47. Rb3 Qxb3 48. Qxa5+ Kb7 49. Qd8 Qe6 50. f3 d5 51. exd5 cxd5 52. Qa5 Qd7 53. Qb4+ Kc7 54. Qd4之后形成的后残局并不简单，黑方能否获胜也不明确。

text: Lasker certainly was not confident about this, and, since he generally under-estimated his opponent's chances, he decided that he had a right to achieve more.
zh: 拉斯克想必也没有把握。由于总体上低估了对手的机会，他认为自己可以争取更多。

text: Who would not be tempted here win the e4 pawn n as well? to White's position looks completely hopeless.
zh: 眼看白方似乎已毫无希望，谁会不想顺手再吃掉e4兵呢？

text: 48. Qa1 Qxe4+ 49. Kh2 Rb5 50 Qa2
White threatens both Rxc4+ and Ra7+ followed by Rxg7. This guarantees him at least a draw.
zh: 白方既威胁Rxc4+，又威胁Ra7+后Rxg7，至少可以确保和棋。

text: 52. Kg2 is better; later White has to lose a tempo.
zh: 52. Kg2更好，实战中白方稍后不得不为此损失一个先手。

text: The idea of Black's check is to avert the check with the queen on a5 after 53. Ra7+ Rb7. However, his king is totally exposed and this gives Schlechter the chance to set the opponent new problems. It is difficult to defend such a king in the middlegame.
zh: 黑方这次将军，是为了在53. Ra7+ Rb7后避免白后到a5将军。不过，黑王已完全暴露，施莱希特因而可以不断制造新的难题。在中局保卫这样的王十分困难。

text: With the threat Qa7+.
zh: 威胁Qa7+。

text: If the king were already standing on g2, White could have played 54. Qa6, which is now impossible in view of 54... Qd6+.
zh: 如果白王已经在g2，就可以走54. Qa6；现在却不行，因为黑方有54... Qd6+。

text: The failure of the general offensive in the centre, fatigue from the opponent's never-ending threats all this, apparently, served as a reason for Lasker's making a mistake. However, the Black king has fallen into such a dangerous position that a draw was already the best way out of the position for him. For this he should play 54... Rb7 or 54... Rb8. 55. Qa6 Rb8 Also 55... Rb7 56. Qe6 does not save him.
zh:
中心总攻未能奏效，加上应付对手接连不断的威胁所带来的疲劳，看来共同促成了拉斯克的失误。不过，此时黑王已十分危险，和棋本来就是黑方能够争取的最好结果。为此，他应走54... Rb7或54... Rb8。

**55. Qa6 Rb8**

55... Rb7 56. Qe6同样救不了他。

text: 56. Ra7+ Kd8 57. Rxg7 Qb6 58. Qa3 Kc8 Or 58. Qb4 59. Qa7. In making his last move, Lasker at the same time resigned, without waiting for mate after 59 Qf8+ Qd8 60. Qc5+.
zh:
**56. Ra7+ Kd8 57. Rxg7 Qb6 58. Qa3 Kc8**

若58... Qb4，则59. Qa7。拉斯克走完最后一步便认输了，没有等白方走出59. Qf8+ Qd8 60. Qc5+，形成杀棋。

text: The whole ending serves as an instructive example of the underestimation of middlegame ideas in the struggle e with heavy pieces. Strictly speaking, Lasker made only one, but nevertheless a principal mistake. He yielded too much to the mercy of endgame ideas.
zh: 对局最后这一阶段，是重子斗争中低估中局因素的一个深刻教训。严格说来，拉斯克只犯了一个错误，却是原则性的错误：他过分受到了残局思路的支配。

text: This example reveals sufficiently clearly the peculiarities and difficulties associated with defence and attack in the struggle of heavy pieces. The following ending perhaps even more distinctly illustrates these features and difficulties, and likewise the character of mistakes made in such positions even by 1 masters of the highest class.
zh: 这个例子清楚地揭示了重子斗争中进攻与防守的特点和困难。下面的例子将更鲜明地说明这些问题，也说明顶尖大师在这类局面中可能犯下什么样的错误。

text: The game Lasker-Pillsbury, played in the international tournament at Hastings 1895, reached the diagrammed position
zh: 1895年在黑斯廷斯国际锦标赛的拉斯克对皮尔斯伯里一局，形成了图中局面。

text: White's central pawns are isolated and weak, his king is in need of defence. Black already has an extra pawn, the exchange of any of the pieces makes it easier for him to realise his material advantage in the endgame: in short, he has every chance of victory. This is how both partners assessed the state of affairs during the game.
zh: 白方的中心兵孤立而薄弱，王也需要保护。黑方已经多一兵，无论兑掉哪一对重子，都更有利于在残局兑现子力优势。总之，黑方大有胜机。实战中双方都是这样评价局面的。

text: Admittedly 1 a dynamic assessment of the position points to a certain weakness of the Black a7 and c7 pawns, but the need for White to defend his king and e4 pawn makes it difficult to exploit the minuses in the opponent's pawn skeleton.
zh: 从动态角度看，黑方的a7兵和c7兵确实也有些弱，但白方必须照顾自己的王和e4兵，很难利用对方兵形的缺陷。

text: Let us look at how further events developed in this difficult position.
zh: 下面看看这个复杂局面如何发展。

text: The leap of a wounded tiger! It is reminiscent of the "desperate' play of Schlechter in the previous game. White has nothing to lose and he bravely I goes in for an exchange of his central pawn for the flank one of his opponent. On 23. Qf3, which, possibly, would be preferred by other chessplayers, could follow 23... Qd4+ 24. Kh1 Qg7 with the threat of exchanges on the f-file.
zh: 犹如伤虎奋起一扑！这让人想起上一局施莱希特的“拼命”下法。白方背水一战，勇敢地用中心兵换取对方的侧翼兵。其他棋手或许更愿意走23. Qf3，但黑方可应以23... Qd4+ 24. Kh1 Qg7，威胁在f线上兑子。

text: Pillsbury under-estimates the opponent's s counterchances connected with the passed pawn obtained on the a-file. However, the specific character of play with heavy pieces is such that the presence of such a pawn considerably broadens the possibilities of the side possessing g it. Thus, for example, the queen ending will be acceptable for White, while in some cases, if Black does not manage to blockade the passed pawn in time with the king, even the rook ending. Therefore Pillsbury should prefer 24... c4 after which both 25 Qxc4 Qxc4 26. bxc4 Rb2 and 25. bxc4 Qf2! 26. Rg1 Qb6 27. Qa4 Rf8 28. Qd7 e5 are in Black's favour. He apparently feared another continuation, namely 25. Qc6 Rf8! 26 Rxf8+ Kxf8 27. h3 cxb3 28. axb3 Qc5 29. Qd7 Qxc2 30. Qxe6 Qc1 + 31. Kh2 Qf4+ 32. Kh1 Qf7 or 30. Qxh7 Qxe4 31. Qxc7 Qe1+ 32 Kh2 Qe5+ 33. Kh1 a5. Actually, in both 1 cases, lofty technique would be required to v win, but victory would undoubtedly have been achieved.
zh:
皮尔斯伯里低估了对手在a线获得通路兵后的反击机会。在重子斗争中，通路兵能显著增加己方的选择。例如，白方现在可以接受后残局；某些情况下，只要黑王不能及时封锁通路兵，白方甚至可以接受车残局。因此，皮尔斯伯里应当选择24... c4。此后无论25. Qxc4 Qxc4 26. bxc4 Rb2，还是25. bxc4 Qf2! 26. Rg1 Qb6 27. Qa4 Rf8 28. Qd7 e5，都对黑方有利。

他显然顾虑另一个后续手段：25. Qc6 Rf8! 26. Rxf8+ Kxf8 27. h3 cxb3 28. axb3 Qc5 29. Qd7 Qxc2 30. Qxe6 Qc1+ 31. Kh2 Qf4+ 32. Kh1 Qf7；若改走30. Qxh7，则30... Qxe4 31. Qxc7 Qe1+ 32. Kh2 Qe5+ 33. Kh1 a5。两种情况下，黑方固然都需要很好的技术，但应当能够获胜。

text: 25. Qxa7 Qb7 26. Qa4 c6
The invasion of the queen on d7 was threatened. The insufficiently secure position of the Black king begins to tell.
zh: 白方威胁后侵入d7。黑王位置不够安全的弊端开始显现。

text: The significance of the extra pawn has been appreciably neutralised.
zh: 黑方多一兵的优势已经被大大削弱。

text: This move bears witness to the fact that Pillsbury did not try to understand sufficiently deeply the situation which has arisen.I By removing g the rook from the back rank, he dooms the queen to the role of watchman for the passed pawn.N Meanwhile, in the forthcoming struggle, the energy of the queen is needed for the fulfilment of another task. It is therefore no surprise that soon Black not only proves to be powerless to realise his advantage but also a real threat of defeat hangs over him. The rook move also has another shady side it worsens the position of the Black king, with which the rook now loses contact. In making his aggressive t thrust, Pillsbury obviously counted on enlivening the passed e-pawn and, by threatening to advance it, to avert or to some extent weaken the offensive power of the enemypassed pawn. However, very soon it becomes clear that this plan is mistaken and that the passed a-pawn in the present situation is more advanced and dangerous than the e-pawn. Pillsbury's idea proves to be insufficiently concrete, he cannot foresee, with necessary distinctness, a way of leading to the achievement of the planned objective.
zh: 这步说明皮尔斯伯里没有深入理解局面。他把车调离底线，迫使后留下来看守通路兵；但接下来的斗争恰恰需要后去完成另一项任务。因此，黑方很快不仅无法兑现优势，反而面临输棋的危险。这步动车还削弱了黑王的安全，因为车已无法照应王。皮尔斯伯里积极出击，显然是想活跃自己的e通路兵，用冲兵威胁牵制对方的通路兵。然而，实战很快证明这个计划有误：当前局面中，a通路兵走得更远，也比e通路兵更危险。皮尔斯伯里的构想不够具体，没有清楚看出实现目标的途径。

text: Up to this fatal last move, Pillsbury could still nourish some hopes of realising his material advantage. It was necessary to reinforce the e-pawn from behind, by playing 29. Re8. After the possible 30. a5 d5 31. Qe2 e4 32. Ra1 Qg7! 33. Ra2 e3 34. a6 Qe5 35. a7 Ra8 the chances would still be on Black's side. Even after making a mistake, Pillsbury ought to have immediately corrected it by returning with the rook to b8. Wishing to be consistent, from now on he goes downhill; an interesting chess episode from the psychological point of view.
zh: 走出这步致命的错误之前，皮尔斯伯里仍有希望兑现子力优势。他应走29... Re8，从后方支援e兵。例如30. a5 d5 31. Qe2 e4 32. Ra1 Qg7! 33. Ra2 e3 34. a6 Qe5 35. a7 Ra8，黑方仍有较好的机会。即使已经走错，他也应立即退车b8加以纠正。但他执意贯彻原来的想法，从此每况愈下。从心理角度看，这一过程颇值得玩味。

text: White threatened 33. Qf2 and, if 33... Qe7, then 34. a7; in short, storm clouds hang over Black's position. Therefore 32... Rb8 was obligatory, after which he could still fight on, but already only for a draw. This is achieved by 33. Qg3 Ra8 34. Ra1 Ra7! 35. Qb8+ Kg7 and there is nothing better for White than to force a draw by 36. Qe5+ Kg8 37. Qb8+, since the continuation 37. Rf1 leads to nothing for him because of 37 . Qe7.
zh: 白方威胁33. Qf2，若33... Qe7，则34. a7，黑方阵地已危机四伏。因此必须走32... Rb8，才能继续抵抗，而且只能争取和棋。以下变化可以说明：33. Qg3 Ra8 34. Ra1 Ra7! 35. Qb8+ Kg7。白方也没有比36. Qe5+ Kg8 37. Qb8+强制和棋更好的办法；若改走37. Rf1，则37... Qe7，白方并无收获。

text: The winning move. White has deprived the Black rook of the possibility of returning tot the eighth rank, and the a-pawn in the end completes its victorious march.
zh: 制胜的一步。白方切断黑车返回第八横线的道路，a兵终于能够一路前进，决定胜负。

text: The White passed pawn achieves its objective first: 34... e2 35. a7. The ill-fated rook on b4 is out of play. On 34... ( Qa7 White simply captures the e3 pawn.
zh: 白方的通路兵抢先一步：34... e2 35. a7，b4车只能置身事外。若34... Qa7，白方直接吃掉e3兵即可。

text: Also 35. Ra2 was sufficient for a win, but he would have to reckon on play with four queens on the board. This is how the finale might be in this case: 35... Qf1+ 36. Kh2 e2 37. a7 e1=Q 38. a8=Q Kg7 39. Ra7+ Kh6 40. Rxh7+ Kxh7 41. Qgc7+ Kh6 42. Qh8+ Kg5 43. Qcd8+ Kf4 44. Qh6+ and Black is mated. It is interesting that this was the only way to win after 35. Ra2. Lasker prefers not to tempt fate, which so surprisingly has smiled on him.
zh: 35. Ra2也足以获胜，但必须算清双方各有双后的变化。可能的结局如下：35... Qf1+ 36. Kh2 e2 37. a7 e1=Q 38. a8=Q Kg7 39. Ra7+ Kh6 40. Rxh7+ Kxh7 41. Qgc7+ Kh6 42. Qh8+ Kg5 43. Qcd8+ Kf4 44. Qh6+，黑方被将杀。值得注意的是，这是35. Ra2之后唯一的取胜途径。好运如此意外地降临，拉斯克不愿再冒险试探它。

text: 35... d4 Or 35... Re4 36. a7 Re8 37. Rxe3 Rc8 38. Qb8 Qf8 39. Qb7 Qf1+ 40. Kh2 Qf4+ 41. Rg3 Qf8 42. Rf3 Qe8 43. Re3! and wins. 36. a7 Qd8 37. Ra1 Qa8 38. Qd6 Rb7 If 38... e2, then 39. Qe6+; on 38... Rb5 follows 39. Ra6.
Since on 40... elQ+ White plays simply 41. Rxe1.
zh: 因为40... e1=Q+之后，白方只须41. Rxe1。

text: The struggle proved to be very instructive in the ending of the 15th game of the return match Euwe-Alekhine (1937).
zh: 1937年尤伟对阿廖欣世界冠军回敬赛第十五局的最后阶段，同样很有启发性。

text: White has a passed pawn, indeed one which is furthermore defended from behind. In the rook and queen endings this guarantees him an indisputable positional advantage.
